papers.title: Stochastic Nonlocal Conservation Laws with Lévy Noise: Stability, BV Estimates, and Vanishing Viscosity
papers.abstract: We study one-dimensional stochastic nonlocal conservation laws with a convolution-type interaction field, driven by multiplicative Brownian noise and compensated Poisson random measures. The nonlocal operator modifies the classical entropy structure, while the jump noise produces nonlinear correction terms in the entropy inequality. We introduce a notion of stochastic entropy solution and establish an $L^1$-stability estimate using spatial doubling of variables and the Itô--Lévy formula. This yields uniqueness in the vanishing-viscosity class and, under additional bounds, a localized Cauchy estimate of order $\sqrt{\varepsilon+\varepsilon'}$. Existence is obtained by vanishing viscosity: we construct the viscous solutions through a Faedo--Galerkin scheme and derive viscosity-uniform $L^1$ and localized $BV$ estimates, which allow us to pass to the limit and obtain a spatially $BV$ stochastic entropy solution.

papers.title: Dualizing involutions on Kazhdan-Patterson covers of $\mathrm{GL}(r)$
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero and $G=\mathrm{GL}(r,F).$ Let $r,n \geq 2$ and $\widetilde{G}$ be an $n$-fold Kazhdan-Patterson cover of $G$. Let $\pi$ be an irreducible smooth representation of $G$ and $\pi^{\vee}$ be the contragredient of $\pi$. Let $\tau$ be an involutive anti-automorphism of $G$ satisfying $\pi^{\tau}\simeq \pi^{\vee}$. In this case, we say that $\tau$ is a dualizing or duality involution. When $r=2$, it is known that any lift of the standard involution on $G$ to $\widetilde{G}$ is a dualizing involution if and only if $n=2$. In this paper, we study the dualizing property of the lifts of the standard involution on $G$ to $\widetilde{G}$ and prove the following: (i) When $r \geq 2$ and $n \geq 3$, we show that any lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ is never a dualizing involution. (ii) When $r=2t$ and $n=2$, we show that any lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ is a dualizing involution. (iii) When $r=2t+1$ and $n=2$, we show that there is a unique lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ which is a dualizing involution.

papers.title: Twisted Fourier-Mukai partners of genus 1 curves
papers.abstract: We study twisted derived equivalence between genus 1 curves over an arbitrarly perfect field.

papers.title: Local well-posedness for the Novikov-Veselov equation at subcritical regularity
papers.abstract: We establish local well-posedness of the Novikov--Veselov equation (NV), at every fixed value of the energy parameter, for initial data in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ in the entire subcritical Sobolev range $s>-1$. The argument is perturbative and does not invoke the integrable structure, instead adapting the strategy in our previous work on KdV (2026). An infinite normal-form expansion indexed by binary trees is combined with a gauge transform that bypasses the obstructions in the associate bilinear estimate, and the resulting gauged equation -- carrying nonlinear contributions of every order -- is closed by a contraction in a Fourier restriction space. The analytic engine is a family of frequency-restricted multilinear bounds, supported by a detailed description of the two-dimensional resonance geometry attached to (NV).

papers.title: Optical Representation Neural Networks Enabled by Weakly Supervised Learning
papers.abstract: Diffractive optical neural networks (ONNs) show remarkable promise in high-speed and energy-efficient optical computing. However, most existing ONNs are optimized to reproduce predefined output intensity distributions, with the desired optical responses explicitly specified before training. Here, we introduce optical representation neural networks (ORNNs) enabled by coarse-grained weak supervision. Using handwritten Devanagari, Arabic, and English characters as three semantic groups, a modified contrastive objective encourages samples from the same script to cluster into similar optical representations. Remarkably, ORNNs improve the classification accuracy by approximately 9% over conventional supervised ONNs, while requiring only around 18% of the training steps to reach a stable test accuracy of 84.5%. These features can be selectively interpreted using corresponding semantic decoders. Building on this concept, we further realized semantic optical encryption with electronic neural network (ENN) decryption using experimentally acquired representations from a single-layer diffractive network fabricated by two-photon polymerization lithography (TPL). Here, we combine information from different scripts into a mixed optical ciphertext that is then first optically classified before being decrypted with a matched ENN. This work broadens the training paradigm of ONNs by coupling upstream optical representation learning with downstream task-specific decoding, opening new avenues for optical information processing.

papers.title: Another step towards spectral descriptions of cyclic functions
papers.abstract: We consider the operator $V_f=M^{*}_{f}M_{f}$ in the weighted Hardy spaces $H^{2}_{\omega}$, with $M_f$ the operator of multiplication by the function $f$. We determine some basic properties like the essential spectrum when $f$ is a polynomial. Then we focus on the point spectrum when $f$ is a degree 2 polynomial and $H^{2}_{\omega}$ is the Bergman space, assuming that certain parameter is real. We show how this bifurcates into two possibilities: in one we establish the lack of eigenvalues while, in the other, the lack of maximal dimension eigenspaces.

papers.title: A Machine-learning-aided Workflow for Sampling Small Polaron Dynamics in Energy Materials
papers.abstract: One of the defining characteristics of most energy materials, used as e.g.~battery electrodes, photovoltaics, or photocatalysts, is their ability conduct charges such as electrons and holes. The exact mechanism of this conductivity depends on the material, but is often dominated by the existence of mobile small polarons, i.e.~electrons or holes strongly localised through the polarisation of their environment. Computationally, small polarons can be treated with reasonably accuracy through the use of self-interaction corrected or hybrid density functional theory (DFT) together with local geometry optimisation. Similar approaches can be employed to determine the energy barriers to movement of the polarons through hopping. Unfortunately, realistic energy materials tend have very large numbers of symmetry inequivalent polaronic configurations and correspondingly large numbers of hopping barriers, making them hard to tackle explicitly. In this work we therefore extend the computational reach of DFT calculations with machine-learned (ML) surrogate models, which then feed into a kinetic model to quantitatively estimate the conductivity of a battery anode material (Li$_4$Ti$_5$O$_12$ or LTO) at realistic, defected conditions. We calculate the conductivity at room temperature to be 6.7 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ S/cm which lies well in the experimental range. To this end, we only needed a total of 154 polaron barrier calculations, out of 3649 symmetry inequivalent ones, achieving an over 20-fold increase of computational efficiency. Overall, our work demonstrates how DFT-trained ML surrogates can be used to quantitatively and efficiently sample the dynamics of small polarons in energy materials.

papers.title: Hidden Quantum Markov Processes: Mealy Formulation and Observable Reduction
papers.abstract: We formulate hidden quantum Markov processes in a Mealy architecture using a single completely positive unital transition expectation coupling the present hidden system, the emitted output, and the next hidden system. Together with a boundary state, it generates a quasi-local, finitely correlated hidden--output state; for the commutative generator associated with a classical Mealy kernel, this state is the full joint law of the classical Mealy model. Moore realizations correspond to transition expectations that factor on the prescribed hidden algebra. We establish a rank obstruction to such factorization and prove its sufficiency for isometric generators: factorization holds exactly when the induced hidden-memory channel has Kraus rank at most the hidden Hilbert-space dimension. The Kraus rank also gives the minimal intermediate Hilbert-space dimension. When the hidden and output dimensions are at least two, the factorizable isometric generators form a closed subset of measure zero. For any fixed projective readout, a Mealy generator induces an operational hidden quantum Markov model in the sense of Monràs, Beige and Wiesner; conversely, every finite-dimensional operational model admits a Mealy lift on the same memory space with a rank-one readout. For their cluster-state instrument, two isometric, Moore-factorizable lifts with the same instrument and initial memory state yield identical measured output statistics but different quantum output states: one has marginals entangled across $1|2\cdots n$ for $n\geq3$, with three-output negativity $\tfrac12$, whereas the other has fully separable marginals. Thus operational equivalence does not determine output entanglement.

papers.title: Recursive Semi-Blind Receivers for Wideband Array Processing
papers.abstract: Using the commonly employed uniform rectangular array (URA) as an illustrative example, we have recently shown that the block-term tensor decomposition (BTD) model provides a natural representation for the output signal of a multi-dimensional separable sensor array structure in the presence of channel multipath. A palette of effective and efficient semi-blind joint channel estimation/data detection (JCD) algorithms for URA processing, which wed BTD modeling with existing JCD schemes, has thus been developed, and recently extended so as to be applicable in large-scale arrays and/or time-varying environments. However, both the model and the algorithms were based on the assumption of narrowband signals, arriving through paths of effectively the same delay. In this paper, recursive JCD algorithms for wideband sources are developed and evaluated through simulations in a time-varying setting and across different constellation sizes, in comparison with their batch counterparts and the training-only-based solution. They are seen to enjoy the ability to track channel variations and detect the transmitted symbols `on the fly', with the aid of only a short initial training stage.

papers.title: The ratio of gradient-flow scales $\sqrt{t_0}/w_0$ in $2+1$ flavor lattice QCD
papers.abstract: We determine the ratio $\sqrt{t_0}/w_0$ of gradient-flow scales in isospin-symmetric $2+1$-flavor QCD at the physical point and in the continuum limit. Our analysis uses CLS gauge ensembles at five lattice spacings and combines Wilson and Zeuthen flow data to constrain the continuum extrapolation at the flavor-SU(3)-symmetric point. We obtain $\sqrt{t_0}/w_0=0.8264(26)$ in the Edinburgh consensus scheme, corresponding to a precision of about $0.31\%$. This result relates determinations quoted in terms of either flow scale and helps assess tensions among published results.

papers.title: Symmerty-Engineered Moire Metasurface for Multibeam Control
papers.abstract: Moiré metasurfaces offer a versatile platform for wavefront engineering through the relative rotation of periodic structures. Despite extensive demonstrations of continuous beam steering, the physical mechanisms governing beam multiplicity remain poorly understood, hindering the systematic design of multibeam radiation states. Here, we establish a predictive framework for engineering beam multiplicity in reflective moiré metasurfaces based on the dominant Fourier coefficients of their constituent patterns. We reveal that the rotational symmetry of these Fourier components in reciprocal space fully determines the symmetry of the resulting moiré unit cell and, consequently, its radiation characteristics. By further incorporating their phase information, both beam multiplicity and steering trajectories can be accurately predicted. We demonstrate this approach using reflective moiré metasurfaces constructed from patterns with p6m, p3m1, and p4m plane-group symmetries, achieving one-, two-, three-, four-, and six-beam radiation states with continuously tunable steering trajectories. Beyond symmetry-based design, we identify two additional degrees of freedom for beam multiplicity control. Selecting different rotation centers reshapes the phase distributions of the dominant Fourier coefficients, enabling further manipulation of beam multiplicity and spatial arrangement, while varying the relative twist angle alters the pairing of Fourier components, inducing transitions between distinct beam multiplicities. These findings establish a systematic framework for versatile and reconfigurable multibeam wavefront engineering.

papers.title: Latent resonances in oscillator networks
papers.abstract: In networks of coupled oscillators, from neural circuits to power grids, damping is expected to suppress oscillations because of its dissipativity. Here we show that local damping can, counterintuitively, amplify oscillations along some input-output channels, while the network's global oscillation energy decreases and its spectral properties improve. The amplified oscillation arises from a latent resonance that lies in the spectrum yet barely manifests. The added passive damping reshapes this resonance by mixing it with adjacent eigenmodes. In random power-grid networks, damping can boost weakly responding channels by more than an order of magnitude, while subdominant channels can grow to exceed the originally strongest channel. Damping thus not only suppresses oscillations but also provides a way to redistribute oscillatory energy. For any passive network, the amplified response and its upper bound follow exactly from baseline quantities, offering a principled route for network design and control.

papers.title: Long rational and Gaussian integer multiplication
papers.abstract: Long integer multiplication is a fundamental operation in computational algebra, heavily relying on Toom--Cook and related evaluation-interpolation algorithms. Conventional wisdom dictates that multiplication on the Gaussian integers $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is reduced to standard rational integer multiplication, since $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is a ring extension of $\mathbb{Z}$. We show that this approach is far from optimal and moreover inverting this established paradigm, that is reducing rational to Gaussian multiplication, leads to faster rational integer multiplication algorithms. We introduce a novel Toom--Cook framework that reduces rational long integer multiplication to Gaussian integer multiplication, yielding a strictly more efficient computational pipeline. By taking advantage of the special properties of the rational integer domain inside the Gaussian integers, we achieve a more favourable algebraic structure that reduces the overall arithmetic cost in every metric. To validate this theoretical shift, we provide a complete implementation of our algorithm. Benchmarks demonstrate that our approach outperforms the highly optimised GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library (GMP) by up to 29\%, bridging a fundamental theoretical insight with significant practical improvements in high-performance computer algebra.

papers.title: Second order and secondary functional renormalization group flow equations
papers.abstract: The functional renormalization group provides a powerful non-perturbative framework for quantum field theory through the exact flow equation for the scale-dependent effective action. A mass-type regulator $R_k = k^2$ is particularly attractive because it preserves symmetries, locality, and unitarity (or Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity in the Euclidean domain). However, unlike momentum-dependent regulators, it does not tame all ultraviolet divergences: in four dimensions, flow equations for the effective potential exhibit logarithmic divergences. Motivated by Callan's perturbative renormalization scheme, where higher-order $\theta$-insertions improve ultraviolet convergence, we develop two classes of higher-order functional flow equations. First, we derive exact second-order flow equations by taking further derivatives of the standard flow equation with respect to $k$. These have either a one-loop structure involving the first derivative of the inverse propagator, or a mixed one-loop and two-loop structure. While exact and useful for incorporating two-loop effects and testing truncation schemes, they do not in general resolve the ultraviolet convergence problem. Second, we introduce a secondary flow method, where variations of an effective mass-squared parameter introduce an additional flow, with parameter $l$. The resulting secondary flow equations become ultraviolet finite once sufficiently many derivatives have been taken, and can be evaluated without an additional ultraviolet regulator. Integrating back to the standard flow requires integration constants that encode microscopic ultraviolet physics, analogous to relevant coupling constants.

papers.title: Products of Trees, $Σ$-theory, Higher Baumslag-Solitar Groups
papers.abstract: We study the $\Sigma$-theory of groups equipped with multiple HNN decompositions in the case where the product of the associated Bass-Serre trees satisfies the hypotheses of Brown's criterion. We then obtain an explicit description of the $\Sigma$-theory restricted to the span of all characters dual to one of the HNN decompositions. One consequence is that Meinert's Direct Product Formula holds in this context. As a key ingredient for the proof, we present a purely topological result that allows reading off the essential connectedness and acyclicity properties of products of regular trees with height functions. As the main application of our theorem, we introduce higher Baumslag-Solitar groups. We prove that they admit a canonical system of HNN decompositions, and use it to deduce multiple results, such as the existence of normal forms, and a well-behaved structure of standard parabolic subgroups (which include the vertex and edge groups). By understanding their interplay with a special class of endomorphisms called multiplication maps (which include the structure maps), we control the action on the product of Bass-Serre trees. This allows us to compute the full $\Sigma$-theory of higher Baumslag-Solitar groups.

papers.title: Data-Driven Output Regulation via Predictive Control
papers.abstract: This paper addresses constrained output regulation for unknown linear systems by means of predictive control directly from input-output data. The objective is to reject disturbances and track references generated by a known exosystem, without identifying a plant model or solving the output regulator equations. The first step is a trajectory parametrization for plants driven by exosignals with known dynamics. % By exploiting the known exosystem eigenstructure, Willems et al's fundamental lemma is extended from autonomous input-output trajectories to trajectories coupled with exogenous modes. By exploiting the known exosystem eigenstructure, input-output trajectories driven by an exosignal of known phase are parametrized directly from data, which contains the affine version of Willems et al.'s fundamental lemma as a special case. This parametrization yields a nominal data-driven predictive control (DDPC) regulator, for which a Lyapunov argument proves exponential convergence to the regulator manifold. For periodic exosignals, the steady-state feedforward input is eliminated from the online problem through an incremental-input regularization, leading to an implementable regulator based on measured data and known exosystem information. Bounded output noise is handled by slack and coefficient regularization, with a regularization center computed offline from data; the resulting robust DDPC law is recursively feasible and practically stabilizing, with an ultimate regulation error that vanishes with the noise bound. A constrained lateral vehicle-control example with periodic road curvature illustrates disturbance rejection, input-constraint satisfaction, and the transition from exact regulation with noise-free data to practical regulation with noisy data.

papers.title: Metastable vortex string decay in a brane picture
papers.abstract: We describe the decay of a metastable string as a bounce in a brane configuration. We consider a particular $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric $\mathrm{U}(2)$ gauge theory with cascade Higgsing $\mathrm{U}(2)\to \mathrm{U}(1)^2 \to \mathrm{U}(1)$, where the vortex string can break by creating a pair of 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole and anti-monopole. The theory is engineered in a Type IIA brane setup, where the metastable string is realized as a D2-brane stretched between NS5- and D4-branes. The string breaks when the endpoints of the D2-brane, moving along the NS5- and D4-branes, meet so that the D2-brane shrinks to nothing. We check that the tension of the D2-brane reproduces that of the vortex string obtained numerically in the field theory, with the ratio approaching one in the limit where the vortex string becomes BPS. Within the thin-wall approximation, we derive the bounce action from the Dirac-Born-Infeld action of the D2-brane and find that it agrees with that of the field theory, with the monopole mass given by the area swept by the D2-brane. As a consistency check, we numerically construct a bounce solution of the D2-brane equation of motion under simplifying assumptions, whose action agrees with the thin-wall result in the regime where our description is reliable.

papers.title: Two correlation scales in homogeneous density-matrix functionals: the Müller logarithm and the sharp Csányi--Arias asymptotics
papers.abstract: We resolve the exact high-density correlation scales and coefficients of the three-dimensional translation-invariant, spin-symmetric Müller and Csányi--Arias corrected Hartree--Fock (CHF) functionals, settling long-standing numerical observations of Müller overcorrelation and apparently vanishing CHF correlation. In Hartree units, for fixed spin multiplicity $q$ and Fermi momentum $k=(6\pi^2\rho/q)^{1/3}$, their gains per particle over the filled Fermi sea satisfy \[ D_{\rm M}(k)=\frac{3}{4\pi^2}\log k+O(1),\qquad D_{\rm CHF}(k)=12e^{-1/2-\pi^2/8} k^2e^{-\pi^{3/2}\sqrt{k}}(1+o(1)). \] The Müller proof retains the occupation cap and identifies the factor-of-two cancellation between exchange defect and energy gain. For periodic Müller jellium, convexity and translation--spin averaging allow a global minimizer to be chosen invariant and identify the unrestricted thermodynamic energy with the homogeneous spin-symmetric value. The CHF upper bound follows from a deterministic comparison built from the explicit Hartree--Fock dispersion, combining a full Birman--Schwinger bound with one-sided norms and completion of the square; a number-preserving trial state provides the matching lower bound, and the retained remainder yields weighted $L^2$ convergence of the occupation defect without analyzing the self-consistent gap. We also prove existence for both functionals and uniqueness of the CHF minimizer. Relative to the unpolarized quantum high-density benchmark, Müller has a larger logarithmic coefficient, providing quantitative evidence for the conjectured Müller lower-bound property, whereas CHF misses the logarithmic scale altogether. The quantum benchmark is not used in either functional proof.

papers.title: Stable projective immersions of Kähler metrics with some radial symmetry
papers.abstract: We combine Calabi's criterion with Pringsheim's theorem to study projective inducibility under positive rescaling. By restricting to suitable radial holomorphic curves, we obtain an obstruction to local Kähler immersions into finite- or infinite-dimensional complex projective space that applies uniformly to every positive rescaling. For invariant rational curves, we show that non-rationality of the moment map implies that no positive rescaling is projectively induced. We apply these criteria to the Taub-NUT, Candelas-de la Ossa, non-flat Stenzel, and Hwang-Singer scalar-flat metrics, as well as to Gibbons-Hawking metrics. Except for the Burns-Simanca metric in the Hwang-Singer family, no positive rescaling is projectively induced. For Gibbons-Hawking ALE spaces with at least two centres, the conclusion holds in every compatible complex structure. We also extend the results to complex space forms of arbitrary curvature with at least one finite signature index.

papers.title: Resolving the isospin-mixing anomaly in $^{26}$Si from $^{26}$P $β$-decay
papers.abstract: The $\beta$-delayed one- and two-proton emission of the proton-dripline nucleus $^{26}$P provides a sensitive probe of isospin symmetry-breaking. A recent study reported the observation of a strongly isospin-mixed doublet in $^{26}$Si, comprised of the $T = 2$ Isobaric Analog State (IAS) and a state at 13380 keV, yielding a record-high isospin mixing matrix element. We report a new high-resolution measurement of the $^{26}$P $\beta$-delayed charged-particle decay performed at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB), shedding new light on the isospin mixing in this decay. By utilizing low-energy beam implantation from the Advanced Cryogenic Gas Stopper (ACGS), we obtained clean one-proton and two-proton decay spectra. Our high statistics study show discrepancies in decay branches and the existence of a 13380 keV state in $^{26}$Si is unsupported by our data. Our deduced branching ratio to the IAS is fully consistent with the expectation from the Fermi sum rule. Consequently, the claim of strong isospin mixing in $^{26}$Si is refuted, reinstating standard theoretical expectations for isospin mixing in nuclei.

papers.title: Constant-Weight Sparse Vector Coded Augmented-AFDM
papers.abstract: Sparse vector coding (SVC) and its variants convey information through sparse vectors (SVs), or sparse support patterns and detecting information by solving sparse recovery problems, making them attractive for short-packet ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC). However, as the required information rate increases, conventional SVC schemes or the enhanced SVC (ESVC) schemes require a rapidly growing number of SVs, resulting in significant increase of complexity and receiver processing latency. On the other hand, when communicating in doubly selective channels, orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) suffers from the Doppler spread induced inter-carrier interference, while affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) experiences the same peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) problem as OFDM, although it allows diversity gain from channel's double selectivity. To address these issues, this paper proposes a constant-weight sparse vector coded augmented AFDM (CW-SVC/A$^2$FDM ) scheme, along with a corresponding joint support and symbol detection algorithm. In this scheme, SVs are represented by constant-weight codewords that feature a fixed Hamming weight and a large Hamming distance, resulting in relatively small SV sets. Simulation results compare various SVC/ESVC schemes and diverse coding schemes employed by the CW-SVC/A$^2$FDM, including Hamming, BCH, RS, and polar codes, for QAM symbol protection. The results demonstrate that the proposed scheme provides a distinct reliability advantage over conventional SVC/ESVC schemes, achieving a gain of up to 14 dB. Furthermore, the study indicates that the CWC's weight and minimum Hamming distance must be carefully selected to balance detection reliability, QAM modulation order, and sparse recovery feasibility, thereby maximizing the overall system's performance.

papers.title: ADfiRe: An empirical- and CFD-informed advection-diffusion-reaction thermal model for wildfire spread
papers.abstract: Real-time wildfire forecasting requires a trade-off between rapid yet physically relevant models and high fidelity but computationally costly models of flame spread over heterogeneous, multiphase solid fuel. The present study introduces ADfiRe, a hybrid framework that integrates empirical correlations and CFD-informed parameterizations into a physics-based advection-diffusion-reaction (ADR) formulation. The key features of ADfiRe are the use of established fuel databases, the capacity to handle multiple fuels, and a methodology to capture the effect of arbitrary topography. Furthermore, it includes the effect of flame tilting due to wind, thus accounting for the differences between plume- and wind-dominated fire propagation. ADfiRe resolves explicitly the coupled thermochemical degradation as well as heat and mass transport mechanisms of the advancing fire front. The wind field is modeled based on an appropriately defined Byram number. The model is validated against five well-documented experimental field-scale fires in Mediterranean shrublands, showing quantitative agreement with key metrics such as the rate of spread (ROS) and the fireline intensity, through a two-stage, Arrhenius-based heterogeneous reaction scheme coupling solid-fuel pyrolysis and oxygen-limited char/volatile combustion.

papers.title: Higher derived limits, Kurepa families and Chang's Conjecture
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between homological algebra and combinatorial set theory, specifically focusing on the (non)vanishing of higher derived limits of certain inverse systems of abelian groups, denoted $\mathbf C_{[\kappa]^\lambda}$, indexed by the ordered sets $([\kappa]^{\lambda},\subseteq)$, where $\lambda < \kappa$ are infinite cardinals. Our first main result is a general structural theorem which provides a generalisation of Goblot's theorem to the setting of locally small directed sets. We then present the first systematic study of generalised cofinal Kurepa families. We establish their existence in the constructible universe $L$ and under specific cardinal arithmetic hypotheses. Then, we apply our structural result to show that $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[\kappa]^{\aleph_n}} = 0$ in environments where the appropriate cofinal Kurepa families exist. In contrast, we explore conditions that force these derived limits to be nonzero. In particular, we prove that certain instances of Chang's conjecture (CC), together with the existence of suitable $\diamondsuit$ sequences, imply that $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[\kappa]^{\aleph_n}} \neq 0$ for appropriate values of $\kappa$. Adapting forcing techniques from Eskew and Hayut, we construct models of these instances of CC together with the required $\diamondsuit$ sequences, establishing the consistency, for each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, of $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[\aleph_{\omega_n}]^{\aleph_n}} \neq 0$.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Control of Magnetoconvective Flows via Differentiable Simulation
papers.abstract: Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) fluid flows are central to demanding engineering applications, most prominently fusion blanket cooling, where flow control is a promising tool to optimize key properties such as heat transfer. While active flow control (AFC) has recently advanced through machine learning, its application to MHD flows remains largely unexplored. In this work, we present $\phi$-PICT, a novel differentiable GPU-accelerated MHD solver targeted at AFC. We validate $\phi$-PICT against MHD benchmarks and demonstrate its high computational efficiency. Integrated into FluidGym, $\phi$-PICT enables sample-efficient gradient-based algorithms to improve heat transfer by $>25$% and allows optimizers to achieve $10^3\times$ higher accuracy in inverse design than black-box methods. $\phi$-PICT is publicly available at this https URL .

papers.title: Emulating spatially extended systems using Fourier Neural Operator
papers.abstract: Operator Learning (OL) algorithms approximate underlying mathematical operators by mapping entire classes of input functions to their corresponding solutions. For instance, architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) have been trained on numerical datasets generated by isolated, stiff ionic models to provide a data-driven alternative to traditional numerical integration schemes. However, real-world biological and physical systems typically consist of interconnected spatial units arranged in complex, heterogeneous networks. Motivated by this observation, we generalize this data-driven framework to spatially extended systems defined on diverse graph topologies, ranging from Erdos-Renyi to Barabasi-Albert networks. Furthermore, we evaluate the proposed approach on empirical data, demonstrating its ability to accurately and efficiently model task-oriented neural activity.

papers.title: Existence and regularity for a non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation with a confining potential
papers.abstract: We study the non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation $\operatorname{div}(Du/\sqrt{1-|Du|^2})-V(x)u+|u|^{p-2}u=0$ in $\mathbb R^N$, where $N\ge3$ and $2<p<2^*=2N/(N-2)$. For a $C^1$ potential satisfying $\inf V>0$, $V(x)\to\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$, and $|x\cdot\nabla V(x)|\le C_DV(x)$ with $0\le C_D<p-2$, we prove the existence of a positive classical solution and infinitely many distinct nontrivial classical solutions. The argument combines the nonsmooth monotonicity trick with compactness induced by the confining potential. A Pohozaev-type identity yields uniform bounds for parameter-dependent critical points. A local minimization characterization identifies these critical points with weak solutions and establishes strict spacelikeness. Local Schauder estimates then give $C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity. All the solutions belong to the natural energy space $H_V^1(\mathbb R^N)$ and satisfy $|Du|<1$.

papers.title: The cone of states over time: exact tests and convergent two-sided hierarchies
papers.abstract: A state over time (stote) pairs a state $\rho$ with a channel $\mathcal{E}$ as the Hermitian, generally non-positive operator $(\rho\otimes\mathbf{1})\star J_\mathcal{E}$. We study the convex cone $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$ generated by these operators. Our main result is a convergent outer semidefinite hierarchy with an explicit trace-norm Hausdorff bound on its trace-one slices. Specializing constrained symmetric-extension theory to the input--channel representation, we show that Bose-extension rounding preserves the channel marginal constraint and gives error at most $2d_A^2(d_A-1)/(k+d_A-1)$ at level $k$. A complementary inner hierarchy retains all channels at each chosen pure-input direction. For $d_A\ge2$, its error is at most $2(d_A-1)\sin^2\delta$, where $\delta$ is the Fubini--Study covering radius; nested sets of $N$ directions give error at most $2\pi^2(d_A-1)N^{-1/(d_A-1)}$, independently of $d_B$. These bounds provide explicit size--accuracy guarantees and certified support-value bounds, without guaranteeing finite termination for exact boundary membership. For binary classical outputs, we obtain an exact SDP membership test, including indefinite output blocks and mixtures that are not single stotes. At faithful marginal the test reduces to a scalar inequality; every trace-one member of this sector with input marginal $\rho$ has a constructive realization using at most $\operatorname{rank}\rho$ pure-input stotes with binary measurement channels. Finally, we compute the exact isotropic boundary and prove $\mathrm{PPT}\subsetneq\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\cap\mathrm{PSD}\subsetneq\mathrm{PSD}$ for equal local dimensions at least two.

papers.title: Dimensionalities on monoids
papers.abstract: We study equivalence relations on monoids in $\Rel$ that are lax morphisms. We call them \emph{dimensionalities}. We prove that the quotient of a monoid in $\Rel$ by a dimensionality is again a monoid. We prove that polygroupoids (and hence hypergroups) are exactly the symmetric $†$-Frobenius structures in $\Rel$. We use this characterization to prove that the quotient of a polygroupoid by a dimensionality that preserves the inverse is a polygroupoid.

papers.title: Additive cubes are avoidable over $\{0,1,2,3\}$, $\{0,1,4\}$ and $\{0,2,5\}$
papers.abstract: We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over the alphabet $\{0,1,2,3\}$, thereby solving a long-standing question initiated by Pirillo and Varricchio in 1994. By extending the reduction and spectral machinery of Cassaigne, Currie, Schaeffer, and Shallit (2014), we prove that the search for additive cubes in such morphic images reduces to a finite graph traversal. We exhibit eight explicit morphisms from $\{0,1,3,4\}^*$ to $\{0,1,2,3\}^*$ of length 3 whose images on the Cassaigne \textit{et al.} infinite word contain no additive cubes.

papers.title: Symbolic Regression Fitting for Roche Lobe Radius
papers.abstract: We present a compact approximation to the dimensionless, volume-equivalent Roche lobe radius $R_{\rm L}/a$, obtained by applying symbolic regression to radii calculated from the full Roche potential. Over $10^{-5}\leq q\leq10^5$, the expression reduces the root mean square error from $1.97\times10^{-3}$ for Eggleton's formula to $5.95\times10^{-4}$, while its maximum relative error is $1.39\%$, compared with Eggleton's $0.83\%$. Calculations at additional mass ratios give a mean relative error of $0.331\%$. The formula is monotonic, recovers the $q^{\frac{1}{3}}$ scaling at small mass ratio, and approaches a large-mass-ratio limit within $0.036\%$ of the limiting Roche model. In a NumPy float64 benchmark of $10^7$ direct formula evaluations, the SR expression takes $0.217$~s compared with $0.450$~s for Eggleton, a speed-up of $2.08$. These results quantify the accuracy and evaluation cost of a compact algebraic alternative for binary-system calculations.

papers.title: WISE-VAULT: Decade-long Mid-Infrared Variability of WISE AGN
papers.abstract: Mid-infrared (MIR) variability provides a powerful probe of accretion processes and dust reprocessing in active galactic nuclei (AGNs), as it is less affected by extinction than optical flux. Using multi-epoch photometry from \textit{WISE} and NEOWISE spanning over a decade, we investigate the MIR variability of $\sim$4.5 million color-selected AGNs. Variability is quantified using maximum--minimum amplitudes ($\Delta W1$), excess variance, reduced $\chi^2$, and structure function (SF) analysis over timescales of 0.5--10 years. We identify 632,939 variable AGNs, including 54,897 sources that exhibit large-amplitude variability ($\Delta W1 > 0.5$ mag) and 624 with extreme intrinsic variability ($A_{\rm var} > 0.5$ mag). A subset of these sources shows flare-like behavior, identifying them as candidate changing-look AGNs or tidal disruption events that warrant further spectroscopic and multi-wavelength follow-up. The SF analysis shows radio-detected AGNs exhibit the highest variability amplitudes, followed by X-ray detected and the overall AGN sample. The variability amplitude is strongly anti-correlated with the Eddington ratio, indicating enhanced variability in lower accretion rate systems. A weak positive dependence on radio-loudness further suggests a contribution from non-thermal emission in radio sources. These results demonstrate that MIR variability provides a robust diagnostic of accretion physics and an efficient means of identifying extreme and rapidly evolving AGN phenomena. The full catalog of variable AGNs is made publicly available.

papers.title: Asteroseismology of blue straggler stars in $ω$ Centauri. Stellar collisions as a possible formation scenario
papers.abstract: Context. Blue stragglers are intriguing stars that appear more massive and younger than expected from single-star evolution, yet their evolutionary histories remain elusive because of the multiple possible formation channels. A promising and poorly explored avenue for addressing this problem is asteroseismology, which provides the most stringent constraints on internal structure and evolution. Aims. We investigate five SX Phoenicis stars from the core of the globular cluster \omega Centauri that pulsate in two radial modes and occupy the blue-straggler region of the colour-magnitude diagram. Seismic models are constructed assuming a collisional origin and compared with our previous seismic studies based on single-star evolution. For comparison, we also explore a binary-evolution scenario involving mass transfer for one of the stars. Methods. The evolution of the parent stars is computed with MESA. The collision is then modelled with the MMAMS code, which reconstructs the merger remnant using an entropic variable. The subsequent evolution is followed with MESA up to the current age of the cluster. Finally, we construct seismic models reproducing the observed frequencies of the two radial modes. Results. We present the first seismic modelling of SX Phe stars (blue stragglers) based on the collision-formation scenario. Convective-core overshooting is essential for rejuvenation and for obtaining seismic models in the main-sequence phase of evolution, but it is not always sufficient. Whether a merger remnant undergoes rejuvenation depends in a complex way on the masses of the parent stars, metallicity, and collision time. We identify three evolutionary behaviours: no, delayed, and immediate rejuvenation. The collisional seismic models imply younger ages and higher masses than the seismic models based on single-star evolution.

papers.title: Essential spectrum of singularly perturbed Dirac operators on bounded domains
papers.abstract: In this paper self-adjoint Dirac operators on bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$ with elliptic boundary conditions perturbed by singular $\delta$-shell potentials supported on compact curves or surfaces are considered. While the unperturbed operator has purely discrete spectrum, it is shown that certain critical values of the interaction strengths lead to the appearance of essential spectrum. More precisely, each connected component of the interaction support, where the coupling constants have such critical values, produces in dimension two a point and in dimension three even a closed interval in the essential spectrum, where the size of the latter depends on the geometry and the coupling constants.

papers.title: On character conductors and Sylow p-subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$, where $G$ is a finite group and $p$ is a prime, and let $\chi\in\operatorname{Irr}(G)$. In 2024, I. M. Isaacs and G. Navarro asked whether the degree of $\mathbb{Q}_{p^f}$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p(\chi_P)$ is always at most the $p$-part $\chi(1)_p$ of $\chi(1)$, where $p^f$ is the $p$-part of the conductor of $\chi$ and $f\geq1$. Here $\mathbb{Q}_n=\mathbb{Q}(e^{2\pi i/n})$ is the $n$th cyclotomic field, $\chi_P$ is the restriction of $\chi$ to $P$, and $\mathbb{Q}_p(\chi_P)$ is the field generated over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ by the values of $\chi_P$. We prove that this inequality holds for $p$-solvable groups.

papers.title: ESME stays positive: event generation with positive weights
papers.abstract: Fully differential simulations of hard-scattering processes are a cornerstone of precision phenomenology at collider experiments. For long, Monte Carlo event generators have been able to achieve next-to-leading order (NLO) accuracy, but their results typically suffer from the presence of negative-weight events. These degrade statistical power and complicate downstream analyses. In this contribution, we present Exponentiated Subtraction for Matching Events (ESME), a novel approach to NLO+PS matching that yields positive-definite event weights while preserving perturbative accuracy and the logarithmic structure of the shower. We discuss the formalism and its implementation within the PanScales framework.

papers.title: The Exact Stabilization Time of Self-Stabilizing Coloring: Mean, Variance, and Distribution
papers.abstract: The worst-case stabilization time of a self-stabilizing algorithm usually says little about its typical behavior beyond the order of magnitude. This paper revisits the classical self-stabilizing $Delta+1$ coloring algorithm with vertices activated at random, one at a time (the random central daemon). Considering the number of color changes as a random variable, we study its mean, variance and, on several families of graphs, its exact distribution. The analysis rests on a reduction: a vertex changes color, at most once, exactly when it is not a local maximum of a uniformly random labeling of the vertices, maxima being taken among the neighbors that share its initial color (the monochrome initial configuration is the slowest case). What can be predicted depends on what is known of the graph. The degree distribution (the view at distance one) gives the mean. The variance needs the view at distance two, in particular the triangles, and the full law needs the whole graph. We give closed-form results, from monochrome and from uniformly random initial configurations, on paths, cycles, random trees, Erdős-R{é}nyi graphs and bipartite random graphs. From a monochrome start, the mean stays within a factor two of the worst case, whereas the variance ranges from zero (disjoint cliques) to order $n^2$ (the star on $n$ vertices)..

papers.title: A Concise Introduction to Quantum Electromagnetics
papers.abstract: This book introduces quantum electromagnetics to readers trained in classical electromagnetics, without assuming a systematic background in quantum mechanics. The central question is when classical descriptions suffice, and when the quantum states of matter or the field must be retained explicitly. Starting from familiar electromagnetic modes and material response, the discussion develops atomic dynamics, field quantization, and the interaction of quantized fields with quantum matter. Particular attention is given to how mode profiles, Green functions, and scattering matrices obtained from classical electromagnetic calculations enter quantum models. Atomic coherence, photon statistics, spontaneous emission, and cavity coupling are developed through derivations that identify the physical assumptions and limits of each description. Examples drawn from atomic clocks, Rydberg-atom receivers, and single-photon devices connect these concepts to excitation, propagation, and measurement in practical systems. Loss and noise are included in relating internal dynamics to measured signals and correlations. The final discussion examines how sensitivity and claims of quantum advantage depend on bandwidth, measurement resources, and the classical reference used for comparison. The aim is to help readers choose an appropriate model, carry out the calculation, and understand what its predictions mean for an electromagnetic measurement.

papers.title: The Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment: classical and quantum optimization approaches
papers.abstract: Efficient railway rolling stock management requires the coordinated planning of train-unit assignment, shunting movements, track occupation, service operations, and workforce allocation. These interdependent decisions give rise to a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly as the size of the fleet and the planning horizon increase. This paper introduces the Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment, a mixed-integer linear programming formulation that integrates these operational decisions within a unified optimization framework. To improve computational tractability, a preprocessing procedure is developed to reduce the size of the resulting model. The proposed approach is evaluated through computational experiments on instances of increasing size and under different objective-function weight and cost configurations. Classical optimization experiments using Gurobi show that filtering method reduces the number of decision variables and constraints, while its impact on computational time varies across instances. In addition, a constrained quadratic model representation is investigated using D-Wave's hybrid quantum-classical optimization solver.

papers.title: Menu Design Meets Market Design: Strategic Simplicity vs. Choice Complexity
papers.abstract: Strategic simplicity removes the incentive to misreport preferences, but it does not ensure that participants can identify what they prefer. We study this distinction in a laboratory experiment on serial dictatorships, where optimal play only requires choosing one's favorite bundle of real-effort tasks. Participants make fifteen incentivized choices among bundles that vary in how many tasks they combine. They choose either from a large menu or through a series of binary choices. Having made all choices, they unexpectedly reconsider each assignment against a previously rejected alternative. We find that roughly one in six choices is reversed and almost one in five involves an objectively dominated bundle. Simplifying the choice architecture does not help. Binary decomposition even raises reversal rates among low-ability participants and further inflates their confidence about their choices.

papers.title: BeST: Beta splatted tomography for direct reconstruction from coherent imaging measurements
papers.abstract: Conventional coherent X-ray tomography requires the phase of each projection to be reconstructed with high fidelity. However, individual reconstructed projections might be flawed, e.g. due to positioning errors, yielding inconsistent tomographic reconstructions. By directly coupling phase retrieval and tomography, consistency is enforced through a common object volume. But reconstructing a full volume demands substantial computational resources. To reduce this demand, we introduce Beta Splatted Tomography (BeST), which represents the common object volume using compactly supported beta primitives with closed-form analytical projections, enabling efficient reconstruction directly from coherent scattering images. This representation substantially reduces the number of optimizable parameters compared to a voxel grid. We demonstrate BeST on experimental datasets from hard X-ray near-field holography and far-field ptychography measurements. In both cases, the joint technique improves reconstruction quality compared to two-step methods.

papers.title: Flow structure, heat transport, and dissipation in vertical-field magnetoconvection at similar Reynolds numbers
papers.abstract: We employ direct numerical simulations to investigate the effect of a vertical magnetic field on the flow structures, heat transport, and dissipation rates in Rayleigh--Bénard convection of a low-Prandtl-number fluid ($\mathrm{Pr} = 0.025$) at an approximately fixed Reynolds number ($\mathrm{Re} \approx 880$), maintained by adjusting the Rayleigh number to compensate for the Lorentz force. As the Hartmann number increases, the flow becomes more anisotropic, which strengthens the positive convective heat fluxes relative to the negative ones and thereby raises the Nusselt number, accompanied by a thinning of the thermal boundary layers. The total viscous and thermal dissipation rates are dominated by the boundary layers, whereas the total magnetic dissipation rate is dominated by the bulk. With increasing Hartmann number, the boundary-layer fraction of the viscous and magnetic dissipation rates increases, whereas that of the thermal dissipation computed from the temperature fluctuations decreases, owing to the suppression of temperature fluctuations near the boundary layers. The dissipation rates deviate from log-normality and are well described by stretched exponential distributions, whose tails become more extended with increasing Hartmann number.

papers.title: General $δN$ formalism in Single Field Inflation and Graph Theory
papers.abstract: We study higher order correlation functions in single field inflation using the $\delta N$ formalism and methods from graph theory. By representing connected tree level contributions as graphs, we systematically classify their independent topologies, momentum shapes and amplitudes. We show that the amplitudes of arbitrary trees factorize into products of primary amplitudes, providing a general framework for relations among higher order correlators, including the Suyama-Yamaguchi equality. As the number of external legs increases, the number of distinct tree topologies grows exponentially, whereas the number of algebraically distinct amplitude products grows considerably more slowly. As an application, we consider ultra-slow-roll inflation followed by a transition to a slow-roll attractor. For transitions without a potential step, we derive an explicit all-order expression for the vertex amplitudes and establish their positivity and dependence on the sharpness of the transition. When a potential step is included, we prove that all nonlinear vertex amplitudes remain positive for upward steps, whereas downward steps allow cancellations at specific parameter values. These cancellations can eliminate entire families of tree contributions, including configurations in which the leading local bispectrum and trispectrum vanish simultaneously while higher order correlations remain nonzero.

papers.title: Superregular Breathers in the Sasa--Satsuma Equation: Spectral Conditions and Modulation Instability
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the superregular breathers (SRBs) of the Sasa--Satsuma (SS) equation by combining a Darboux construction with a linear stability calculation. The reduction symmetry of the scalar SS Lax pair makes the fundamental SRB construction degenerate. The paired quasi-Akhmediev branches nevertheless yield second-order SRBs in the focusing sector $n|_{\gamma=0}<0$; neither the defocusing sector nor the focusing sector $n|_{\gamma=0}\geq0$ supports this construction. Linearization about the same plane-wave background gives the modulation-instability gain and, on the admissible branches, reproduces its relation to the group-velocity difference. The carrier wavenumber $b$ enters through the background rather than as a coefficient of the SS equation, and changes the spectral roots and instability interval. In the formal NLS limit, the result reduces to the familiar NLS gain. Numerical evolution of finite-width periodic perturbations produces the predicted second-order profile over the displayed propagation interval.

papers.title: A Multiobjective Optimization Framework for Sensor Array Design in Magnetocardiography
papers.abstract: Magnetocardiography (MCG) noninvasively measures cardiac magnetic fields. Conventional cryogenic systems use fixed multichannel arrays, whereas room-temperature sensors enable flexible placement to reduce array size and measurement redundancy. The present study aims at developing a scheme to identify the optimal sensor placements by utilizing three methodological sensor optimization frameworks such as physics driven, experimental data driven and a hybrid combination of both. The physics-driven method optimizes continuous planar coordinates using D-optimality, spatial correlation, and leastsquares error. The data-driven method uses measured spatiotemporal fields and pole-geometry metrics, while the hybrid method integrates both approaches. The evaluation is performed using training objective, Pearson correlation, normalized root-meansquare error (NRMSE) and pole separation(mm), orientation(°) and trajectory(mm) errors, where physics-driven optimization identified 16 sensors with a correlation of 0.9914 and an NRMSE of 0.0139, with pole separation, orientation, and trajectory errors of 3.71 mm, 1.38°, and 3.55 mm, respectively. Data-driven optimization shows diminishing improvements beyond 17 sensors, achieving correlation 0.9840, NRMSE 0.0035, and pole errors of approximately 4.30 mm, 1.70°, and 6.80 mm. The hybrid method achieves correlation 0.9945 and NRMSE 0.0201 with 14 sensors, reducing sensor count by 12.5% relative to the physics-driven configuration. Its pole errors of 6.50 mm, 2.31°, and 7.50 mm satisfy the study-defined thresholds, balancing array compactness with magnetic-field morphology preservation. These results show that optimized placement helps alleviate the complexity of data redundancy and enhances the performance of MCG as a routine cost-effective clinical measurement.

papers.title: Enhancing Transient Stability of VSG-Controlled Converters Under Grid Frequency Disturbances
papers.abstract: Strong damping feedback can substantially improve the transient synchronization stability of renewable energy converters employing virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control. However, conventional damping feedback uses the nominal frequency as its reference. When the frequency of a weak grid deviates from nominal, strong damping tends to keep the VSG frequency near nominal. This can sustain a frequency difference between the VSG and the grid and compromise transient synchronization. To address this problem, this paper proposes a complex-frequency-based method to estimate the grid reference frequency from local terminal measurements. The estimated frequency replaces the nominal reference in the VSG synchronization loop, so that damping acts on the frequency difference between the VSG and the real grid. Controller hardware-in-the-loop tests validate the effectiveness of the proposed method under grid frequency disturbances and its robustness to grid parameter uncertainty and adverse grid conditions.

papers.title: Few-Shot Open-Set Hyperspectral Pixel-Wise Classification with Spatial Aware Label Propagation
papers.abstract: Pixelwise classification of hyperspectral images (HSI) is a fundamental task in remote sensing, but its deployment in real-world applications is often limited by the scarcity of labeled data and the presence of unknown classes at inference time. In this work, we propose Few-shot Open-set hyperspectral recognition from Self-Supervised Learning training (FOSSeL), a unified framework for few-shot, open-set hyperspectral pixelwise classification that does not require supervised training. The proposed approach first leverages self-supervised learning to construct a discriminative feature space from unlabeled data. Then, given a small set of labeled seed pixels, class predictions are obtained through spatially-aware graph-based label propagation over superpixel representations, enabling the joint exploitation of spectral similarity and spatial consistency. To address the open-set scenario, we introduce simple yet effective strategies to identify pixels that do not belong to the known classes. We evaluate FOSSeL on three benchmark hyperspectral datasets under multiple few-shot settings. The results show that the proposed framework achieves competitive or superior performance compared to fully supervised methods while maintaining robustness in the presence of unknown classes. These findings highlight the potential of combining self-supervised feature learning with graph-based inference for practical HSI analysis in low-annotation and open-world scenarios.

papers.title: Wireless Node Ranking via Fourier-Driven Maximum-Likelihood Estimation (extended version)
papers.abstract: We apply non-abelian Fourier theory to the problem of maximum-likelihood estimation of the order of a line topology, based on signal strength measurements under shadowing only. This yields up to a 60-fold speedup over standard methods for uncorrelated shadowing. Moreover, for correlated Gaussian shadowing with a singular covariance (e.g. the joint path-loss model), maximum-likelihood recovery is exact and independent of the shadowing variance (an infinite Le Cam threshold), which our implementation confirms for $\sigma/\alpha$ as high as 7.0. The key object is the covariance's null space. Its dimension is fixed by the topology; its orientation depends on the correlation function only through the per-link variances. Although the mechanism formally requires an exact line, it is robust to small perturbations of the formation: an approximate kernel recovers as well as the exact one. We explore the dependence on the perturbation in detail for five nodes.

papers.title: Evidence for a Fast, Long-Period, Hot Population of Accreting Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: Context. Accreting neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries allow us to probe the accretion histories that produce recycled millisecond pulsars. Aims. We expand the analysis of the spin distribution with an enlarged sample of 39 accreting neutron stars and investigate whether the high-frequency objects preferentially occur in binaries with longer orbital periods and have higher quiescent surface temperatures. Methods. We compare several empirical models for the spin distribution. We use stochastic drift-diffusion estimates and simple braking models to determine whether short-timescale torque fluctuations or secular spin-down can account for the observed population widths. Results. The best statistical description of the spin distribution consists of a broad low-frequency component and a narrow high-frequency concentration centred at ~566 Hz with a width of ~32 Hz. Fast rotators preferentially occupy longer orbital-period binaries, with possibly higher neutron star temperatures. Short-timescale stochastic accretion torque fluctuations cannot produce the observed spin-frequency dispersion in either the fast or the slow component, even under generous assumptions. We show that a non-linear deterministic braking mechanism can instead shift and compress a spin distribution, but the spin data alone do not identify the braking mechanism. Conclusions. The population widths appear to reflect differences in long-term torque conditions and/or evolutionary histories rather than short-timescale torque noise. If the fast systems are close to spin equilibrium, their narrow distribution requires the combination of physical parameters setting the equilibrium frequency to vary relatively little from source to this http URL model that explains the spin distribution should therefore also explain why the fast systems tend to have longer orbital periods and, possibly, higher temperatures.

papers.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of the spherically averaged density $\widetilde \rho$ for fermionic bound states of the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ with nuclear charge $Z$. For the density associated with an eigenfunction satisfying $H_{N,Z}\psi=E\psi$, we show that if the energy $E$ is below the bottom of the essential spectrum $\Sigma:=\inf\mathop{\rm this http URL } (H_{N,Z})$, then \[ \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln \widetilde \rho(r)}{r} =\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{d}{dr}{\ln \widetilde\rho(r)} =-2\alpha_0, \] with $\alpha_0=\sup\{\alpha \ge 0\colon e^{2\alpha r}\widetilde \rho \in L^1(\mathbb{R_+},r^2dr)\}$. The same is true at threshold in certain cases. Moreover, we prove $\alpha_0^2=\Sigma-E$ for the ground states of $H_{3,Z}$ with sufficiently large $Z$.

papers.title: Lower bounds on ranks of universal quadratic forms through geometry-of-numbers
papers.abstract: We obtain lower bounds for the ranks of universal forms over totally real cubic fields using techniques from geometry-of-numbers and the parametrisation of cubic rings by binary cubics due to Delone--Faddeev. Additionally, our methods give lower bounds for totally real primitive fields of any degree with codifferent generated by a totally positive element.

papers.title: Spectral dependence of Berry phase and topological bound states in the continuum in Möbius resonators
papers.abstract: The Möbius strip and the bulk Möbius resonator are of great interest to specialists in optics, acoustics, and quantum physics. Despite the apparent simplicity of the object and numerous publications, the Möbius resonator, like a magic box, still holds many surprises. Here, we demonstrate experimentally, theoretically and with a simple illustrative example that in a "thin" Möbius resonator with an odd number of twists, the longitudinal wavenumber is determined by the additional phase shift {\pi} (traditionally called the geometrical Berry phase) only if the total transverse index of the photonic mode is odd. For an even index, the Berry phase is zero. We also discovered "topological" quasi-bound states in the continuum in Möbius resonators with a square cross-section; they differ from "ordinary" ones by the exchange of azimuthal indices of the interfering modes in the anti-crossing region. Finally, we demonstrate an example of resonant topology by determining the dependence of the Berry phase on the Möbius resonator geometry based on the frequency difference between the eigenmodes of planar ring resonators and those of Möbius resonators. The discovered effects significantly expand our knowledge of the topology of single resonators and promise new practical applications.

papers.title: Common values of linear recurrences related to Ankeny-Brauer-Chowla polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $P_u(X)=XQ(X)(X-u)+1$, where $Q(X)\in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is monic, separabel, has constant term $\pm 1$, and degree $q\ge 1$. Denote $(A_n(u))$ the linear recursive sequence having characteristic polynomial $P_u(X)$ and initial terms $A_0,\ldots,A_{q+1}\in \mathbb{Z}$ such that at least one of them is non-zero. Then there exist effectively computable constants $n_0,u_0$ depending only on $Q(X)$ and $\max\{|A_0|,\ldots, |A_{q+1}|\}$ such that if $|A_n(u)| = |A_m(u)|$ holds for some integers $u,n,m$ with $u>u_0$ and $n\not=m$ then $\max\{

papers.title: Gravitational form factors of $ρ$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD
papers.abstract: We compute the gravitational form factors and mechanical properties of the $\rho$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD, a holographic model of QCD with backreacting flavor and dynamical chiral symmetry breaking. The parameters of the model are taken from an earlier fit to meson spectra and are not adjusted to form factor data. Both mesons are described by a single spin-1 field, and the six form factors are identified from the matrix element of the energy-momentum tensor with two spin-1 states, following the holographic dictionary. We find that $A_0 = J$ and $A_1 = 0$ hold identically in the model, and show that the remaining form factors $E$, $D_0$ and $D_1$ are regular at zero momentum transfer. We compare the form factors of $\rho$ with results from the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model, a light-cone constituent quark model and the hard-wall holographic model. From the form factors, we compute the monopole and quadrupole distributions of energy, pressure and shear force in the Breit frame. The D-term, defined for spin-1 hadrons as the forward value of the combination $\mathcal{D}_0(t)$ of form factors, is found to be $-2.98$ for the $\rho$ and $-7.43$ for the $a_1$ meson. The mass and mechanical radii are $0.81$~fm and $0.89$~fm for $\rho$, and $0.73$~fm and $0.80$~fm for $a_1$.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) : Performance of the redshift measurement and spectroscopic analysis
papers.abstract: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission has issued its first major data release(Data Release 1, DR1), providing a transformative view of the extragalactic sky through deep photometry and near-infrared slitless spectroscopy. This paper presents the Euclid DR1 spectroscopic data set and details the evolution of the spectroscopic processing function (SPE PF) pipeline, which is responsible for the automated analysis of 1-dimensional spectra acquired by the Near-Infrared Spectro-Photometer (NISP). The SPE PF pipeline workflow comprises spectroscopic classification, redshift determination, and the systematic measurement of spectral features. Emission line fluxes are derived using two independent methodologies: direct integration (DI) and Gaussian fitting (GF). For sources exhibiting broad H$\alpha$ profiles (velocity dispersion larger than $1500$ km s$^{-1}$), a dedicated `QSO mode' is implemented to robustly deconvolve nuclear and host galaxy components. The data set was validated by cross-matching Euclid results with external spectroscopic catalogues, specifically Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR1, and through an extensive visual inspection campaign of approximately 4000 sources within the Euclid Deep Field North (EDF-N). For high-quality samples selected in the EDF-N, we find a 98.5\% agreement between Euclid and DESI spectroscopic redshifts. This success rate increases to 98.9\% when incorporating pipeline probability and reliability estimators. (abridged)

papers.title: Toward Interference-Agnostic RF Source Separation
papers.abstract: Separating a radio-frequency signal of interest from a co-channel interference is mostly addressed with specialized separators, each trained for one pair of signal and interference types and therefore relying on a label that a heavily jammed receiver cannot identify. We show that this reliance is not benign: applied to an interference it was not trained on, such a separator usually fails to recover the signal, and in most of the cases we measure it leaves the signal worse than no processing at all. We then train a single separator over every pair, giving it no indication at test time of which one it faces, on two architectures with no component in common: the convolutional WaveNet of the ICASSP 2024 RF Challenge, and a band-split transformer that we adapt from music source separation. Both behave the same way. At the size of one specialized model, the unified separator stays close to the whole models it replaces, keeping the bit error rate close on almost every pair, better on one and worse on another. On an interference absent from every training set, it does as well as the best specialized model, without anyone having to choose which one to deploy.

papers.title: Auto-conditioned Gradient Descent Methods for Multiobjective Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper proposes two linesearch-free algorithms based on steepest descent methods for smooth multiobjective optimization: auto-conditioned steepest descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-SDM) and auto-conditioned normalized gradient descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-NGDM). Both algorithms estimate the local Lipschitz constant from the function values and the first-order information obtained in previous iterations. AC-SDM uses a shared estimate of the Lipschitz constant to construct a scaled steepest descent direction. For AC-NGDM, we use each function's local Lipschitz estimate to normalize the gradient of the corresponding function and construct the descent direction. We prove that every accumulation point of any sequence generated by both algorithms is a Pareto critical point. We also establish convergence rates of $O(1/\sqrt{k})$ for nonconvex objectives and $O(1/k)$ for convex objectives. Numerical results on several test problems demonstrate that AC-SDM and AC-NGDM require fewer iterations and less CPU time than the multiobjective steepest descent method with an Armijo line search and a max-type nonmonotone line search.

papers.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
papers.abstract: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace and normal states have no density matrices, so the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cramér--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.

papers.title: A narrow band method for non-causal discretizations of anisotropic eikonal equations, with adaptive width, sub-and super-solution construction, and quasi-linear complexity
papers.abstract: We describe a narrow band method for numerically solving anisotropic eikonal equations, and more generally static first order Hamilton-Jacobi equations with possibly non-convex Hamiltonians, discretized using standard schemes (semi-Lagrangian, upwind-differences, Lax-Friedrichs). The causality property is not needed, in contrast with the fast marching method. The proposed approach simultaneously builds a numerical sub-solution u and super-solution u to the problem, and adapts the width of the narrow band based on their comparison. We prove that (1 + $\epsilon$)u $\ge$ u at termination, where $\epsilon$ > 0 is any given tolerance parameter, and that the worst case complexity is O(N | ln $\epsilon$| ln(N/$\epsilon$)), where N denotes the number of discretization points, and the underlying constant is explicit in terms of those associated with the scheme properties. Numerical experiments illustrate our results.

papers.title: Numerical experiments on sunspot penumbral flows
papers.abstract: We present 3D radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulations of sunspots with a self-consistently generated penumbra. We analyze the impact of resolution, surrounding opposite-polarity fields and subsurface large-scale flows on the structure and stability of the simulated penumbra. Extended penumbral filaments are obtained for a subset of the simulations. These were run at 25 km (15 km) horizontal (vertical) resolution and with initial conditions favoring fields with strong horizontal components in the penumbral region. The surface velocities in these simulations are consistent with observations of Evershed flow. The main driving mechanism remains the same as illustrated previously in Rempel (2012). The most successful simulations produce extended penumbrae using a potential magnetic field top boundary, in contrast to previous simulations of extended penumbra with an artificial enhancement of horizontal magnetic field at the top boundary.

papers.title: $B \to D$ form factors from light-cone sum rules
papers.abstract: We present a light-cone sum rule (LCSR) analysis of the $B\to D$ transition form factors $f_+^{BD}(q^2)$ and $f_0^{BD}(q^2)$ in the large-recoil region, including the next-to-leading-power corrections at tree level. The non-perturbative input is provided by the leading-twist $D$-meson distribution amplitude determined from lattice QCD in the heavy-quark large-momentum effective theory (HQLaMET) framework, which enters together with the twist-three and twist-four distribution amplitudes of the $D$ meson fixed by the QCD equations of motion. A combined fit to the LCSR results at $q^2\lesssim2$~GeV$^2$ and to the FNAL/MILC and HPQCD lattice data at $q^2\gtrsim8.5$~GeV$^2$, performed in the model-independent Boyd-Grinstein-Lebed (BGL) parametrisation, allows us to obtain the form factors over the whole physical range and to extract $|V_{cb}|$ from the semileptonic $B\to D\ell\nu$ decay as well as the lepton-flavour universality ratio $R(D)$.

papers.title: Projection of massive and interacting conformal theories to the future null infinity
papers.abstract: On a four-dimensional, globally hyperbolic and asymptotically flat spacetime, we consider a real, linear, massive scalar field. Within the framework of perturbative algebraic quantum field theory and inspired by the principle of perturbative agreement, we regard the mass term in the underlying Lagrangian as an interaction potential. This allows us to construct the algebra of observables of the massive theory and, using a Møller map, to represent its elements as formal power series in the squared mass, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Following [DMP06], we use the bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massless theory to project each coefficient to future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$.In four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, we prove convergence of the projected series in the presence of an infrared cut-off and show that the global adiabatic limit exists but is trivial. We circumvent this obstruction by exploiting the time-slice axiom, which allows us to restrict our attention to observables localized in a causally convex neighbourhood containing a Cauchy hypersurface. Removing the cut-off locally yields a non-trivial limit and hence a bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massive theory. We then extend our procedure to a self-interacting real scalar field. We represent interacting observables as formal power series in the coupling constant, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Each coefficient in the domain of the bulk-to-boundary map can thus be projected to future null infinity. As a concrete example, we apply this method to the stress-energy tensor of a massless scalar field with a quartic self-interaction, computing its projection up to first order in perturbation theory.

papers.title: Mapping NGFS Climate Pathways to GICS Sectors: Application to Portfolio Decarbonization
papers.abstract: Portfolio climate alignment is limited by the mismatch between asset managers' sector classifications and those of climate scenarios. This article proposes an NGFS-GICS mapping based on the materiality of Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions rather than on semantic similarity. The mapping feeds a Sectoral Decarbonization Approach that down-scales NGFS trajectories into GICS sector pathways at portfolio level, adjusted for regional exposure. Applied to two illustrative ETF indices, it shows how sectoral composition and regional trajectories shape a portfolio's financed emissions pathway. The framework is transparent, asset-class agnostic and usable for internal exercises such as climate stress tests.

papers.title: Benchmarking superconducting quantum processors with percolating entanglement quality
papers.abstract: The capability to create large entanglement resources is a key performance attribute of quantum processors, and the size of the resource is often used as a benchmark of processor scale. Recent graph-state experiments have reported entanglement clusters spanning entire chips with hundreds of qubits. However, cluster size alone does not capture the entanglement quality of individual couplings or differences in coupling topology. Here, we introduce percolating entanglement quality (PEQ), a topology-normalized benchmark based on conditional two-qubit negativity and a topology-specific bond-percolation threshold. As an experimental demonstration, we prepare a native graph state on a 64-qubit square-lattice superconducting processor with defects, identify a 52-qubit entanglement cluster, and evaluate the PEQ of the processor. Applying PEQ to previously reported chip-wide graph-state measurements on heavy-hex-lattice processors, we show that PEQ differs substantially among processors whose entanglement clusters span the entire chip. PEQ provides a single chip-wide score without selecting a best-performing qubit subset or path. This score allows processors with different coupling topologies to be compared on a common scale and can inform the design of coupling topologies for scalable chips.

papers.title: Efficient representations by PEPS: critical free-fermion and chiral topological states
