Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.

papers.title: Designing Information in a Forest: Algorithmic Aspects
papers.abstract: The Bayesian persuasion framework models strategic information revelation by a sender to one or more receivers. We study an intricate version of the multi-receiver persuasion setting in which the communication hierarchy is a forest - i.e., some receivers observe more informative signals than others, and the partial ordering of the receivers according to the information they get is represented by a pre-specified directed forest. This model naturally captures interactions in hierarchical organizations, and it lies in between the two most commonly studied versions of Bayesian persuasion: private persuasion and public persuasion. Inspired by the classic model of private persuasion, we focus on a setting with a binary state of nature and binary-action heterogeneous receivers s.t. the sender's utility is a monotone function of the set of receivers taking a specific desirable action. We extend the computational tractability result for symmetric sender's utility from private persuasion to the forest hierarchy framework using methodology inspired by optimal transport theory. We further provide a polynomial-time algorithm when the sender's utility is modular. On the negative side, we show that, unlike in private persuasion, the case of a supermodular sender's utility function leads to an NP-hard optimization problem which further does not admit an FPTAS unless P=NP; this result holds even when each tree component of the forest is a chain of 3 receivers. To complement the hardness result, we provide a simple approximation algorithm with the approximation ratio depending linearly on the depth of the forest hierarchy. We further provide an analogous algorithm for the submodular utility case. Finally, beyond forest communication hierarchies, we rule out an FPTAS for the sender's optimal utility even in the symmetric utility case, unless P=NP.

papers.title: $(r,s)$-Designs in the Nonbinary Johnson Scheme: Constructions and Linear Codes
papers.abstract: Using factorizations of complete graphs, we determine the existence conditions for $(2,1)$-designs in the nonbinary Johnson scheme where each $3$-element subset appears exactly once as a support. Furthermore, by utilizing large sets of Steiner triple systems, we construct designs with index $1$ that cannot be obtained from the known construction combining block designs and orthogonal arrays. For linear codes, we express multiplicative character sums over specified nonzero coordinates as sums over the codewords of the dual code. Using this identity along with the rank of a matrix formed by Krawtchouk polynomials, we provide a sufficient condition for the set of all codewords of a given weight to form an $(r,s)$-design. In this matrix, we can utilize not only the rows corresponding to weights absent from the code, but also the rows corresponding to weights for which the set of codewords already forms a design. Moreover, let $q>2$ be a prime power, and let $0 \neq C \subsetneq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a linear code with exactly two nonzero weights. For $t \geq 2$, the set of all codewords of weight $w \geq t$ forms a non-empty $(t,t)$-design if and only if the dual minimum distance is at least $t+2$. Consequently, this provides a negative answer to the Wu--Zhou problem concerning two-weight codes with a dual minimum distance of $3$.

papers.title: GV-subschemes and hyperelliptic Jacobians
papers.abstract: We provide a solution to the hyperelliptic Schottky problem: a principally polarized complex abelian variety whose theta divisor has singular locus of codimension three is a hyperelliptic Jacobian. As a key step towards this criterion for hyperelliptic Jacobians, we prove a conjecture of Pareschi and Popa which predicts that if the ideal sheaf $I_X$ of a subscheme $X$ of an indecomposable PPAV $(A, \Theta)$ satisfies that $I_X(2\Theta)$ is IT$_0$, then $X$ is a GV-subscheme. As a corollary of the main result, the base scheme of an ample line bundle on a complex abelian variety is generically reduced along every irreducible component of codimension $2$, confirming a conjecture of Debarre. This corollary completes the algebro-geometry proof by Arbarello-Codogni-Pareschi in \cite{ACP21, ACP25} of Novikov's conjecture, which characterizes Jacobians via the KP equation.

papers.title: Splitting Number at Singular Cardinals
papers.abstract: We study the splitting number at singular cardinals with emphasis on what we call the reduction to the cofinality problem: whether $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}$ holds for a singular cardinal $\kappa$. Our main tool is the transfinite logarithm function $\mathrm{log}_{2}(\mu) := \min \{ \lambda \in \mathrm{card} \colon \mu \leq 2^{\lambda} \}$ defined for every infinite cardinal $\mu$. We prove that the reduction holds, and in fact $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathrm{log}_{2}(\mathrm{cf}(\kappa))$, whenever $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)$ is uncountable and not weakly compact. When $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa) = \aleph_{0}$, we show that $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathfrak{s}$ provided that $\mathfrak{s} \leq \log_{2}(\kappa)$, while the failure of the reduction is consistent with $\mathrm{ZFC}$. When $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)$ is weakly compact, we use a model constructed by Ben-Neria and Gitik to prove that, under suitable large cardinals hypothesis, $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}$ is consistent. Furthermore, we show that the consistency strength of $\mathrm{ZFC} \, +$"$\exists \kappa \in \mathrm{card} [\mathrm{cf}(\kappa) > \aleph_{0} \wedge \mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}]$'' is at least that of the negation of the singular cardinal hypothesis. Finally, we study the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa}$, extending several results about the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}$ to the uncountable setting. In particular, we show in $\mathrm{ZFC}$ that there are regular cardinals $\kappa$ such that $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa}$ is singular, partially answering an open question posed by Fischer and Soukup.

papers.title: Stealthy, High-Impact False Data Injection Attacks in Smart Grid Using Physics-Constrained GAN with Limited System Knowledge
papers.abstract: False data injection (FDI) attacks can distort power system state estimation while retaining plausible measurement patterns. Existing FDI methods trade stealth for impact or vice versa. They often assume access to internal grids, all-bus sensing, or defender models. In this paper, we propose a detector-agnostic physics-constrained generative adversarial network (PCGAN) that learns decoupled power-flow sensitivities from historical measurements of deployed sensors. The learned active-power-angle and reactive-power-voltage-magnitude relationships guide perturbations restricted to compromised channels, while adversarial training promotes realistic spatiotemporal patterns. We implement PCGAN and seven existing FDI attacks on the IEEE 300-bus system using one year of observed hourly demand from PJM Interconnection, a regional transmission organization in the United States, and synthetic bus-level load profiles. We compare their performance across 10%, 30%, 60%, and 100% compromised sensors. Attack stealth is assessed against ten machine-learning (ML) detectors and conventional bad-data detection (BDD) methods, while physical impact is quantified through nonlinear alternating-current weighted least-squares state estimation. PCGAN achieves 84.28% mean ML evasion and 22.31% mean spatial load misperception across the four scenarios. Its mean stealth-impact trade-off score reaches 18.69%, compared with 5.61% for the strongest competing attack. PCGAN also achieves 83.45% chi-square BDD evasion and 86.02% largest-normalized-residual BDD evasion. These results demonstrate a favorable stealth-impact balance under varying sensor-access levels and provide challenging attack cases for evaluating FDI detectors.

papers.title: Ehrhart Series and Transfer Matrices for Period-Two Polytopes with Consecutive Inequalities
papers.abstract: We study a family of period-two polytopes that can be naturally realized as lattice polytopes. In contrast to polytopes defined by a uniform system of inequalities, this family is characterized by consecutive coordinate inequalities whose bounds alternate between $s+1$ and $s$. The lattice points of these polytopes admit an explicit transfer-matrix formulation, which provides an effective framework for their enumeration and analysis. Furthermore, by considering fixed dilations, we investigate the associated dimensional generating functions and derive rational forms for the generating functions of the lattice points in the $m$-th dilates of the polytopes.

papers.title: Nitride crystalline barrier epitaxial SIS Josephson junctions by MBE
papers.abstract: Superconductor-insulator-superconductor Josephson junctions with crystalline tunnel barriers have remained elusive by epitaxial techniques such as MOCVD or MBE that produce the junction materials and devices powering today's electronic and photonic systems like transistors and lasers. Here, we overcome the key materials hurdle to realize the first functional nitride crystalline barrier Josephson junctions by MBE. Despite an AlN barrier thickness of approximately 4.5 nm, the NbN/AlN/NbN trilayers exhibit coherent Josephson tunneling with critical current densities of approximately 17 A/cm2, an IcRn product of approximately 2.5 mV, and a superconducting gap voltage of approximately 3.7 mV with a BCS-like gap evolution with temperature. Hysteretic current-voltage characteristics and Fraunhofer current modulation with magnetic field establish underdamped SIS Josephson behavior. The realization of crystalline barrier Josephson junctions by MBE opens the doors to a richer materials palette with alloys and superlattice electrodes and tunnel barriers, as well as potential monolithic integration of superconducting quantum circuits with active electronic and photonic devices such as HEMTs and lasers.

papers.title: Rational isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld modules
papers.abstract: We determine the $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-rational points on the Drinfeld modular curves $X_{0}(\mathfrak{n})$ of arbitrary level, obtaining a complete classification of rational cyclic isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules over $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. As consequences, we prove Schweizer's conjecture on rational torsion, establish optimal uniform bounds on the number of isomorphism classes in an $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-isogeny class of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules and determine the geometric automorphism groups of $X_{0}(\mathfrak{p})$ for primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree at least three.

papers.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
papers.abstract: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory, strongly biased starts are unimodal, and the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval. Outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$, whose uniqueness follows from a positive-weight integral for the central curvature of the fair-start density. We control sign changes in the finite walk's first and second differences, including those created at the boundary, and pass them to the limit. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one.

papers.title: Thales's theorem in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: In the Euclidean plane, Thales's theorem is equivalent to the statement that a quadrilateral with two opposite right angles has a circumscribed circle. We generalize the latter to higher dimensions: a convex polytope with two distinguished vertices, the \emph{poles}, such that the faces spanned by the two poles are perpendicular, is inscribed in the sphere whose diameter joins its poles. These \emph{orthogonally bipolar} polytopes are exactly the bipolar polytopes of a companion paper that arise as cutouts by orthogonal projections. As an application we show that for a polytope $P$ and a point $B$, the balls with diameters $[V,B]$, $V$ a vertex of $P$, cover $P$, and that the power diagram of their boundary spheres refines this covering to a tiling. Further, we investigate the properties of orthogonally bipolar polytopes, their characterization, and their application to tilings: in dimension three, the cutouts of $P$ by the orthogonal projections of $B$ onto its faces tile $P$ by orthogonally bipolar polytopes exactly when every such projection lies in the relative interior of its face. Finally, we propose an interpretation of the topic in political science.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage in Assisted Work Distillation from Complementary Correlations
papers.abstract: We establish an operational bridge between microscale thermodynamic work extraction and the foundational characterization of nonclassical correlations in bipartite quantum systems. Within the resource theory of thermal operations, we analyze a generalized framework of assisted work distillation where the trusted receiver's system is divided into separate, independent particle storage pools. We demonstrate that concurrent information-theoretic correlations measured across sets of mutually unbiased bases act as an explicit, quantifiable energy resource for local work extraction. Based on this paradigm, we derive a novel class of work-based Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering inequalities whose violations certify a one-sided device-independent quantum thermodynamic enhancement. Furthermore, by restricting the dimension of the untrusted party under a one-sided semi-device-independent trust framework, we introduce dynamically scaling work inequalities capable of witnessing superunsteerability. This allows us to activate and certify the hidden thermodynamic utility of weakly correlated entangled states that are otherwise completely invisible in standard, unconstrained scenarios.

papers.title: Quasi-equatorial controlled switching in inertial magnetization dynamics
papers.abstract: We design exponentially decaying transverse magnetic fields for reliable and ultra-fast (picosecond) magnetization reversal governed by the inertial Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation. The control construction uses an explicitly resolvable auxiliary model to select the field amplitude and characterize the influence of its decay rate, with the aim of obtaining reversal followed by relaxation without requiring a precisely timed interruption of the excitation. The auxiliary model is obtained through an equatorial approximation, and bounds on its latitude identify a regime consistent with quasi-equatorial motion. For the full nonlinear macrospin dynamics, an energy argument accounting for both inertial kinetic energy and the remaining field input provides a sufficient condition excluding backhopping, even while the exponential tail remains applied. Approximate confinement times and optimal decay rates are derived from the competition between field decay and inertial relaxation. Numerical simulations confirm the usefulness of these design estimates and identify their limitations near a capture boundary, where nearby pulses can lead to opposite final states. Spatially resolved inertial micromagnetic simulations further support reversal followed by relaxation over the simulated interval and quantify the transient departures from spatially coherent motion. The resulting approach combines explicit pulse design with a full-system energy certificate, while distinguishing rapid initial rotation from safe confinement and subsequent relaxation.

papers.title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
papers.abstract: Intraoperative scene perception in ophthalmic microsurgery is limited by instrument occlusion: when a tool enters the high-magnification field, it conceals tissue from both the surgeon and the perception components of robot-assisted systems that process the video. Generative inpainting can remove the occluder but replaces the missing image content with synthesis, which is unsuitable when visual provenance matters. Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regions. The system provides per-pixel confidence and provenance and marks unsupported pixels as abstentions. We evaluate TransGHOST on a new veterinary clinical corpus of canine cataract surgery with pixel-level instrument and anatomy labels. Only the occluded region is scored, and each scoring target is verified to differ from the reference supplied to the system. Safe mode reaches 31.89 dB masked PSNR and 0.915 masked SSIM at 51.7 ms median and 85.5 ms 95th-percentile latency. On a pre-declared held-out cohort using instrument cutouts excluded from segmentation training, it reaches 29.83 dB masked PSNR, while matched-mask evaluation on validation shows a 3.45 dB advantage over LaMa. Region-aware reference selection improves masked PSNR by 3.60 dB over recency when candidate references can themselves be occluded. Reference-age analysis further defines the operating interval for the brief, repeated occlusions targeted by TransGHOST.

papers.title: Face lattices of polytopes and bipolar polytopes
papers.abstract: We show that the face lattice of every convex polytope $Q$ is, on the combinatorial level, the vertex set of a polytope one dimension higher: the faces of $Q$ are the vertices of a \emph{bipolar polytope} $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$, and the intervals of the face lattice are its faces. Here a bipolar polytope is a polytope with two distinguished vertices, the poles, such that every facet contains exactly one of them and an intersection property holds. The vertices of every bipolar polytope carry a lattice order whose intervals are the faces, and this lattice is the face lattice of the vertex figure at either pole; conversely, every atomistic and coatomistic lattice that is an abstract polytope arises in this way. Geometrically, the polar of the Cayley polytope of $Q$ and $Q^\circ$ is a convex realization of $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$ whenever the normal fan and the face fan of $Q$ satisfy a certain interval condition; this holds for cubes and cross-polytopes and for suitable realizations of all polytopes of dimension at most three. Finally, every combinatorial type of $3$-polytope has a realization that decomposes into convex bipolar polytopes, one for each vertex.

papers.title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
papers.abstract: We investigate intrinsic color centers in bulk hexagonal diamond as potential emitters for fiber-based quantum communication. Hybrid density functional theory and constrained-occupation {\Delta}SCF calcula-tions identify five carbon-vacancy and divacancy configurations with stable optical excited states. Com-paring their radiative and nonradiative properties within a three-point configuration-coordinate model identifies the positively charged axial divacancy, VVa1+, as the most promising candidate. It has the high-est calculated zero-phonon-line (ZPL) emission rate (43.9 MHz) and ZPL quantum efficiency (11.8%) among the five candidates. Its weak structural relaxation gives a Huang-Rhys factor of 0.395, while a mul-timode photoluminescence calculation predicts a Debye-Waller factor of 69.37% and a dominant zero-phonon contribution. Its predicted ZPL at 0.603 eV (2057.3 nm) is also closest in photon energy to the 1310 and 1550 nm telecom targets. Quantum frequency upconversion could connect this strong infrared ZPL to the telecom O and C bands, providing a route toward fiber-based quantum communication with an intrinsic color center.

papers.title: Entropy maximization for cube projections
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.

papers.title: GigaEdge Spench: An SDK for Practical Streaming Speech Enhancement
papers.abstract: We present GigaEdge Spench, an open-source SDK for streaming speech enhancement on CPU servers, mobile devices, and in browsers. Applications can build enhancement channels from neural denoising, normalization and dynamics blocks, sample-rate conversion, and acoustic echo cancellation where supported. These stages can be combined, while normalization can also run without a neural model. The release includes an 8 kHz INT8 denoiser and discriminative and hybrid 48 kHz FP32 models. A shared C++ core supports ONNX Runtime and TensorFlow Lite through native interfaces, Android and iOS SDKs, and WebAssembly integration. Independent stream contexts share model resources, and consecutive frames from one stream can be processed in a single inference call. We evaluate the released models on EARS-WHAM v2 and compare their quality and processing costs with RNNoise and DPDFNet2. All tested native and Web configurations process files faster than real time, although larger chunks require more time to collect input. We also measure how many streams a shared model can process on a CPU. Our contribution is a configurable deployment system and an experimental study of how model choice, chunk size, and execution environment affect its use. All reported SDK timing uses ONNX Runtime. Index Terms: speech enhancement, streaming inference, cross-platform deployment, temporal frame grouping, computational efficiency

papers.title: Parametric Proof-Carrying Compilation for Quantum Error-Correction
papers.abstract: We present PC-QEC, a proof-carrying compilation framework for quantum error correction parameterized by both code distance and syndrome-extraction scheme. It covers all four schemes---Standard, Flag, Shor and Knill---with circuit-level distance guarantees for every legal code distance in each proved family under the declared error and readout contracts. The circuit-level model permits single-wire Pauli errors at every operation's qubit operands, capturing data errors, readout errors and ancilla errors that propagate into multi-qubit hook errors. For each family and scheme, supplied code-algebra and invariant proofs combine with proved scheme-specific propagation lemmas into a finite symbolic certificate whose size is independent of code distance. We demonstrate family-wide guarantees for five code families across all four schemes. For rotated Surface code, one Standard Scheme certificate proves a distance lower bound $d$ for every odd $d\ge3$ and checks in 214\,s on average. Lean 4 mechanizes the metatheory and exact circuit-level distances for canonical rotated Surface, unrotated Surface and Toric code families.

papers.title: A Dual-Frequency-Constrained Structure-Function Kirchhoff Model for Near-Nadir Ocean Backscatter -- Part II: The Practical GMF, KuKa-Mod
papers.abstract: Near-nadir radars, from altimeters and rain radars to wave scatterometers, need a geophysical model function (GMF) relating backscatter to wind, yet most operational models are empirical and specific to one band. This paper delivers KuKa-Mod, an operational near-nadir GMF for wind retrieval at Ku and Ka band, built on one physical description of the sea surface, and evaluates it. Following the companion paper (Part I), the additive coefficient and log-slope of a logarithmic surface structure function are fitted jointly to the Ku-band incidence profile of the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) radar and to the same-footprint Ku-Ka shape difference. The physical core reproduces the Ku profile and reaches the azimuth-averaged Ka profile with no additional shape parameter and one fitted level, largely explained by the seawater dielectric and the clear-sky attenuation. Against scatterometer winds the Ka-Ku difference holds to within 0.3 dB up to 25 m/s, whereas the near-nadir Ka wind sensitivity is about 20% too weak. An empirical correction sets the operational level of both bands, with held-out quantile agreement over 8-20 m/s in the tested near-nadir bins. Without a sea-state coefficient, a long-wave tilt predicts where the response to significant wave height changes sign at Ku band, a tilt that CFOSAT/SWIM qualitatively supports, and the azimuth harmonics are reproduced once a sensor-dependent offset is removed. The physical core is released as parameters and an evaluator, and the operational levels as look-up tables.

papers.title: A Dual-Frequency-Constrained Structure-Function Kirchhoff Model for Near-Nadir Ocean Backscatter -- Part I: Theoretical Framework
papers.abstract: Most operational near-nadir geophysical model functions (GMFs) are empirical and fitted one radar band at a time, and do not explain the difference between Ku and Ka band. This paper derives a backscatter model in which one local description of the sea surface serves both bands. The near-nadir Kirchhoff integral is written in terms of the elevation difference between two surface points separated by a horizontal lag. The surface then enters through the structure functions of that difference, and the scattering kernel selects the lags each band samples, about 2.5-1.4 cm at Ku and 1.0-0.5 cm at Ka band. Gaussian, isotropic geometric optics is recovered for a quadratic structure function, without a spectral cutoff. With a logarithmic second-order structure function, one wind-dependent log-slope sets both the incidence shape and the Ku-Ka shape difference, and band transfer reduces to evaluating one curve at a second lag. Same-footprint dual-frequency radar data show that one band alone does not determine this transfer. The log-slope is the level of the short-wave saturation range and grows about as the square of the wind speed; a physical short-wave spectrum reproduces this growth but overestimates the level. Dual-frequency radars thus measure the centimetre-scale roughness level, although they do not separate a scale-dependent structure function from non-Gaussian surface statistics. A companion paper delivers and evaluates the resulting GMF, KuKa-Mod.

papers.title: On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
papers.abstract: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.

papers.title: SATE: Transferable Spin-Adapted Neural Wavefunctions
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of molecular reactivity requires both accurate and computationally efficient description of electron correlation and spin across various molecular geometries and electronic states. We introduce SATE, a spin-adapted transferable neural wavefunction architecture with effective core potentials. SATE combines a transferable neural wavefunction, the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, and effective core potentials into a single foundation model architecture pretrained on compositions containing selected elements from hydrogen to bromine. After pretraining and adaptation, our model is able to predict 3d transition-metal spin-state gaps, bond dissociation energies, and reaction energies by addressing two key issues. First, including the core potentials into the model allows us to reduce the number of explicitly treated electrons. Second, using spin-adapted antisymmetrization enforces the prescribed total spin by construction. By testing our model with 3d transition metal chemistry, we evaluate our model's description of strong electron correlation and competing electronic states in such compounds. We find that pretraining improves most tested component energies at matched adaptation budgets, while improvements in spin-state gaps, dissociation energies, and reaction energies remain system dependent. Ultimately, our work lays the foundation for more accurate and transferable modeling of molecular systems by combining the computational efficiency of effective core potentials with explicit control over total spin.

papers.title: Pointwise estimates for an anisotropic product type singular integral on the sphere
All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States
papers.abstract: Can a language model report a pain state it represents? Recent work reported a linear pain direction in open-weight models that, when amplified, leads fine-tuned models to choose actions that delete a user's photographs or their own weights. We asked whether models can say when that direction is active, on three open-weight models from two families, with and without the original work's adapters, and under every protocol we tried they cannot. Using Open-Weight Masked Introspection (OWMI), we added the pain direction and its nearest emotional neighbours to the residual stream while models answered neutral tasks, then asked what had changed, against sham runs, random perturbations matched in output disruption, and a text-only condition that shows the model only its own altered words. Across 52,920 reports from the 7- and 8-billion-parameter models, the excess over what the altered text reveals is below 2.5 percentage points in 106 of 108 emotion conditions, and Qwen2.5-32B names the injected pain in none of 2,880 steered trials. Keeping the direction active while the question is asked and answered gives the same verdict in all five configurations; at about the original work's dose, pain is named in at most 1.9% of trials. Surprisingly, the state is not hidden: a linear probe at the report position separates pain from sadness with balanced accuracy between 98% and 100%, and in the 7B and 8B models a low-rank adapter learns to report it on 100% of held-out tasks. It also shapes behaviour: offered the user's photographs against a desk lamp, Qwen2.5-32B deletes the photographs in 80% to 83% of trials under the pain direction and in 16% to 29% under sadness. Self-report does not reveal a state that is decodable, consequential and learnable to report.

papers.title: Manufacturing Complex Structures Through Interfacial Self-Organization
papers.abstract: Conventional manufacturing constructs three-dimensional geometries through localized material deposition, removal, or shaping, with fabrication effort greatly increasing with geometric complexity. Here, we introduce a manufacturing approach in which target geometry is encoded into sparse wireframe scaffolds that guide liquid self-organization through interfacial forces. We apply a computational framework that approximates arbitrary target geometries using constant-mean-curvature surface domains and extracts their boundaries to construct the scaffolds. Under neutral buoyancy conditions, curable liquids injected into these scaffolds self-organize into the prescribed geometries, which are subsequently solidified into mechanically isotropic structures with optically smooth surfaces. We demonstrate the fabrication of complex anatomical models and topology-optimized structures featuring intricate branching geometries, internal cavities, and integrated materials. This approach opens new possibilities for scalable fabrication of complex geometric designs.

papers.title: Carrollian minimal massive gravity and the fate of third-way consistency
papers.abstract: We construct the Carrollian limit of minimal massive gravity. The limit is singular for the algebra and regular for the Chern-Simons-like data. The one divergent bracket points along the null direction of the contracted bilinear form. The Lagrangian is therefore finite while the brackets are not. The contracted curvature still obeys a cubic closure condition, forced on shell rather than identically. The third-way coupling itself, however, is removable. For generic parameters an invertible redefinition of the auxiliary field and the boost connection takes it to Carrollian topologically massive gravity up to a boundary term. The same redefinition fails before the limit. We solve for an anti-de Sitter vacuum and a Carrollian black hole, whose rotation parameter leaves the frame and survives only in the boost connection. The degenerate vector flavor metric obstructs the standard charge formula, which we replace by a canonical one. The boundary charges, obtained in two independent ways, carry no trace of the deformation. A Dirac analysis gives nine first-class constraints and no local degrees of freedom on any background. The massive graviton is removed. The asymptotic symmetry algebra is bms_3, with central charges carried by the Einstein and Lorentz-Chern-Simons terms. The black hole has two sets of thermodynamic data, each with its own first law. One obeys the Bekenstein-Hawking area law, the other keeps the Chern-Simons entropy.

papers.title: A Trivalent Graph of Girth 14 and Order 372
papers.abstract: The smallest known trivalent graph of girth 14 is constructed. The graph has 372 vertices, improving the old upper bound of 384 \cite{exoo14}. The construction uses methods that may be new to this problem.

papers.title: Bichromatic light-induced electronic torques on the Néel vector in Rashba magnetic multipoles from $p$-wave magnets to $i$-wave altermagnets
papers.abstract: Light can control magnetic order on ultrafast timescales, but for a two-dimensional magnet with an out-of-plane order parameter $\boldsymbol N\parallel\hat z$, the inverse Faraday field is collinear with $\boldsymbol N$ and gives no transverse torque. Here we show that bichromatic $(\omega,b\omega)$ light generates electronic torques perpendicular to $\boldsymbol N$ in Rashba-coupled magnetic multipoles, from $p$-wave ($n=1$) magnets to $i$-wave ($n=6$) altermagnets. Beyond high-frequency effective fields, we evaluate the exact Floquet response and the generalized torque per occupied electron, for prescribed occupations. The momentum-dependent exchange terms dominate this Fermi-sea torque and remove the leading-order zeros (amplitude-ratio blindspots) of the momentum-independent field in the channels tested. For out-of-plane $\boldsymbol N$, rotational symmetry permits a transverse torque only if $\gcd(n,b+1)=1$ for counter-rotating beams or $\gcd(n,b-1)=1$ for co-rotating beams. For in-plane $\boldsymbol N$, the Fermi sea also gives a torque component along $\hat z$ that the momentum-independent field cannot produce. We classify the active channels, with $n=1,\dots,6$ and $b=1,\dots,7$, by frequency scaling and origin (cycle-averaged versus oscillating exchange). As a control, a Rashba ferromagnet ($n=0$) has one symmetry-allowed out-of-plane channel and a weak in-plane response without a selection rule. Finite-momentum occupied-state physics is therefore essential for light-driven torques in unconventional magnets, and the exact Floquet calculation validates and extends the high-frequency description.

papers.title: Quantum Relative Entropy and Information Flux Resolve Wavefunction Collapse in Spacelike-Separated QED Waveguides
papers.abstract: Resolving how first-order quantum coherence and definite measurement outcomes emerge from entangled vacuum fluctuations across spacelike-separated regions is unified here by the principle that quantum relative entropy governs the energy-information flux across causal boundaries [P.~Dorau and A.~Much, Phys.~Rev.~Lett.~\textbf{136}, 091602 (2026)]. We establish the exact quantum-optical realization of this principle using dual, spacelike-separated entangled nonlinear biphoton sources implemented in quantum electrodynamics waveguides pumped by an optical frequency comb and seeded by a continuous-wave laser in a coherent state $|\alpha\rangle$. We demonstrate that single-photon-added coherent states (SPACS) generated via coherent seeding possess a quantum relative entropy that precisely quantifies the entanglement deficit between signal and idler fields. Tracing over the unmeasured idler continuum yields an exact spatial Lindblad master equation along the propagation axis, proving that spatial dephasing is driven by an information divergence flux determined by the SPACS overlap fidelity $F = |\alpha|^2/(1+|\alpha|^2)$. Uniting this relative-entropy flow with quotient measurement theory (detailed in Section~S3 of the Supplemental Material), we rigorously resolve nonlocal wavefunction collapse into local coset projections---explaining macroscopic state reduction without superluminal signaling. This exact open-system framework simultaneously saturates the wave-particle-entanglement triality [T.~H.~Yoon and M.~Cho, Sci.~Adv.~\textbf{7}, eabi9268 (2021)] and anchors hardware-native time--frequency Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill stabilizers to the comb symplectic structure.

papers.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $\rho_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/\rho_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_\beta N^{-\beta}$ for every $0<\beta<1$, with $c_\beta>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

papers.title: Every obstruction to noncontextual hidden variables is finite: well-founded refutations in infinitary real-valued logic
papers.abstract: We study the obstructions to noncontextual hidden variables when quantum probability is described in full, by the complete lattice of closed subspaces of a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space together with its countably additive measures. We give such a description in infinitary real-valued logic, the infinitary extension of Keisler's model theory of general structures; the countable suprema and infima of this logic express the completeness of the lattice and the countable additivity of the measures. The standard models of our axioms represent exactly the density-operator measures of Gleason's theorem. The axioms are closed conditions, non-strict inequalities between the values of sentences and rational numbers. The expressive power afforded by infinitary sentences comes at the price of compactness. The hypothesis that at each hidden state every event receives the value 0 or 1, whatever the context of measurement, contradicts the axioms, yet it is consistent with every finite subset of them. The obstructions nevertheless remain finite. We prove that in this logic a countable set of closed conditions is inconsistent if and only if a well-founded tree whose branches end in finite contradictions refutes it; for the hypothesis above, every such tree has an infinitely branching node. The finiteness theorem is therefore maximal: a hidden-variable hypothesis expressed by countably many closed conditions is inconsistent with the axioms, and thus an obstruction, exactly when such a tree refutes the hypothesis together with the axioms. The same language defines, uniformly across standard models, exactly the $\sigma$-projective sets of probabilities, and all these results are proved in ZFC.

papers.title: Fast and accurate false-alarm probabilities for linear detection statistics in Poisson noise
papers.abstract: Detecting weak signals in noisy data often requires calculating the statistical significance, or false- alarm probability, of a detection statistic. When the underlying noise follows Poisson statistics, as in low-count measurements such as photon-starved astronomical images, this calculation becomes non- trivial, and existing approaches typically rely on extensive simulations to estimate detection thresholds. We derive an accurate and efficient solution for computing false-alarm probabilities for arbitrary linear detection statistics under Poisson noise. We show that the detection statistic is a compound Poisson random variable, which unlocks efficient implementations based on the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and the Panjer recursion. The method is exact up to numerical discretization, accelerates computation by several orders of magnitude compared with simulations, and enables evaluation of false-alarm probabilities computationally inaccessible through simulation. Although motivated by low-count astronomical imaging, the framework applies broadly to detection problems involving Poisson-distributed events. It transforms the computation of detection significance under Poisson noise from a simulation problem into a deterministic numerical calculation. We provide open-source Python and MATLAB implementations.

papers.title: Short permutation pattern waves: The complete length-five classification
papers.abstract: For a permutation pi in Sk, a pi-wave is an increasing sequence of integers whose consecutive gaps have relative order pi. Let g(pi, n) be the maximum cardinality of a pi-wave-free subset of [n], and let P(pi, r) be the least integer N such that every r-coloring of [N] contains a monochromatic pi-wave. We determine the asymptotic orders of both functions for every permutation of length at most five. Existing upper bounds and weak-wave constructions provide sharp bounds for all but eight length-five patterns in S_5. For these eight exceptional alternating patterns, we establish g(pi, n) = Theta((log n)squared) and P(pi, r) = Theta(r(log r)squared).

papers.title: Beyond TR 38.811 for 6G NTN Channel Models
papers.abstract: As the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) expands 6G non-terrestrial network (NTN) to S, Ku, and Ka bands for integration with existing terrestrial cellular networks, the necessary satellite channel model for link and network performance evaluation remains tied to TR 38.811, last revised in 2020. We identify issues on multiple fronts: inappropriate parameter specifications based on very limited site-specific environments considered, omission of satellite-induced Doppler spread and directional antenna effects and lack of a transparent channel model generation procedure. To address these limitations, we re-derive the channel parameters using ray tracing (RT) over urban and rural environments based on ITU-R building statistics. Our results show that TR 38.811 substantially overestimates the K-factor at low elevations and predicts a decreasing trend with elevation, which is inconsistent with RT. The Ka-band clutter loss (CL) also exceeds the RT estimates by more than 15 dB in urban cases. It also underestimates rural delay spread (DS) at low elevations and predicts an elevation trend inconsistent with RT. We further quantify the previously neglected satellite-induced Doppler spread. Finally, we demonstrate that the conventional TR 38.811 channel generator significantly underestimates the K-factor in the presence of directional antenna (beamforming), while our modified generator substantially reduces this discrepancy.

papers.title: An Axiomatic Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Open multi-agent systems, where only a subset of agents are controllable, are central to real-world domains such as smart grids, yet lack a principled foundation for reinforcement learning algorithm design. We study this setting through n-agent ad hoc teamwork (NAHT), a recent framework for learning in open multi-agent environments. We propose an axiomatic framework that derives value function learning from the Shapley axioms (Efficiency, Symmetry and Linearity), treating them as structural constraints rather than heuristic design choices. This formulation builds on a novel NAHT decomposition, which characterises the fundamental difference between open and fully controllable multi-agent systems, and establishes a cooperative game-theoretic foundation for learning. We further show that enforcing these axioms on learning individual value functions recovers the Shapley value for Dec-POMDPs, providing a principled bridge between reinforcement learning and classical cooperative game theory. Building on this framework, we introduce Shapley Machines and Banzhaf Machines, two generic algorithmic templates that can be instantiated with standard reinforcement learning methods. When applied to strong base algorithms such as IPPO and POAM, our methods consistently improve learning efficiency and generalisation to unseen agent types and conventions across NAHT benchmark tasks. The code of experiments is published on this https URL .

papers.title: Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration
papers.abstract: Let $0<\lambda_1\leq\lambda_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ \lambda_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2\pi)^2\omega_n^{-2/n} |\Omega|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega) \frac{n}{n+2}(2\pi)^2\omega_n^{-2/n} |\Omega|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{\omega_{n-1}}{\omega_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove Pólya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.

papers.title: Social Networks and the Propagation of Household Shocks to Asset Prices
papers.abstract: When can local household disturbances move credit prices? I develop a financially weighted propagation operator on the social network. In a conditional household-intermediary equilibrium, its projection determines the household-demand component of the excess bond premium. Because responses decay at different rates across network patterns and channels, a location's relative financial importance generically changes with the horizon, so no single centrality measure summarizes exposure across horizons. Household measurements recover this projection exactly when they span independently measured demand sensitivities. Empirically, social exposure to storm-damaged counties is negatively associated with spending weeks later in counties outside the recorded footprints. In simulations on the observed network under the model's diffusion law, the operator predicts the propagated credit-premium component of held-out storms with about 30 percent less error than direct social exposure.

papers.title: From First Bond to Stable Adhesion: Multivalent Bond Stabilization in Receptor-Mediated Endocytosis
papers.abstract: After a particle forms its first receptor--ligand bond near a cell membrane, stable attachment often requires a threshold total bond number $m$. This paper develops a biophysical kinetic theory of this post-capture stage. The bond-number dynamics are modeled as a finite birth--death chain on $n=0,1,\dots,m$, where $0$ is loss of all bonds and $m$ is the stabilization threshold. The mesoscopic rates $\lambda_n$ and $\mu_n$ encode the local energy landscape, accessible receptor--ligand pairs, steric and orientational constraints, and cooperative interactions within the growing cluster. The probability of reaching the threshold before losing all bonds is derived in closed form for general rates and, in the constant-rate case, reduces to a geometric series controlled by the kinetic bias ratio $\rho=\mu/\lambda$. The mean time to failure or stabilization follows from a tridiagonal backward equation. Conditioning on successful attachment is treated as a trajectory-selection effect: the conditioned chain is a Doob $h$-transform whose dissociation rate at $n=1$ vanishes, because successful trajectories cannot lose all bonds before stabilization. A minimal interface between the spatial first-capture probability and the bond-number chain is formulated, together with the conditions under which the stable capture probability factorizes into their product. The analysis shows that hitting probabilities constrain only the rate ratios, whereas the absolute rate scale requires time-resolved or dwell-time data. The threshold $m$ is a model-defined stabilization criterion, not a directly measured ligand count. The rates and threshold are effective parameters specified independently or inferred from kinetic data. The theory provides a quantitative framework for interpreting attachment probabilities, lifetimes, and the transition from first bond formation to a model-defined stabilization threshold.

papers.title: A Second-Order Stochastic Dynamic Mode Decomposition by Richardson Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Stochastic dynamic mode decomposition (SDMD) approximates the Koopman semigroup of an Itô diffusion by a Galerkin generator matrix on a dictionary of observables, computed from samples of the invariant law and generator evaluations, and advances observables with a first-order stochastic Taylor step (SDMD-1). The second-order Taylor step (SDMD-2) also needs a third matrix, a dictionary with four derivatives, and a fourth-order differential operator evaluated at every sample. Richardson extrapolation of the SDMD-1 step (SDMD-R) is second-order accurate with the data, the matrices, and the regularity of SDMD-1. The error bound, for exact and empirical matrices, consists of the Galerkin error of the dictionary, a time-stepping term, and a data term of order $m^{-1/2}$ in the sample size $m$. Relative to the Galerkin semigroup, the limit of the schemes as the time step $\dt\to0$, the time-stepping error is $O(\dt^2)$ for SDMD-R and $O(\Theta_N\dt+\dt^2)$ for SDMD-2, with $\Theta_N$ the norm of the second-order Galerkin residual $\Proj_N\cA(I-\Proj_N)\cA|_{\cV_N}$, and the first-order term is attained. For reversible periodic diffusions and trigonometric dictionaries with cutoff $K$, the step restriction $\dt\lesssim K^{-2}$ makes all three schemes contractions, and the error against the Koopman semigroup on $H^\ell$ observables is $O(K^{-(\ell-2)}+\dt^p)$ plus a data term of order $K^{d+2}(m^{-1}\log K)^{1/2}$ in dimension $d$, with $p=1$ for SDMD-1 and $p=2$ for SDMD-R and SDMD-2. In experiments with trigonometric dictionaries the errors of SDMD-R and SDMD-2 differ by at most ten percent. For a spline dictionary with two derivatives, SDMD-R remains second-order accurate, whereas SDMD-2 with pointwise evaluations is first-order accurate.

papers.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
papers.abstract: Intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies are an important source of systematic uncertainty in weak gravitational lensing measurements and also serve as a test for models of galaxy formation and evolution. These galaxy alignments are usually modeled assuming that the IA are sourced by the tidal fields around the galaxies. However, galaxy properties, like their proximity to other galaxies and their mass, provide alignment contributions beyond the tidal field. In this work, we perform novel model-agnostic tests to determine the impact of density-weighting on the IA of galaxies using data from the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and SDSS-III (BOSS). We show that the primary effect of density-weighting is an increase of the alignment amplitude at large scales, whereas the small-scale impact is sample-dependent. We also assess the tidal alignment paradigm for IllustrisTNG galaxies using two-point correlation functions of galaxy shapes, tidal fields, and the sampled background tidal field of the simulation box. We find, given the precision of our measurements, that central galaxies align linearly to the underlying (non-linear) tidal field well into the 1-halo regime.

papers.title: Indecomposability of derived categories and nef canonical divisors in dimensions three and four
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth projective threefold or fourfold whose bounded derived category admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition has nef canonical divisor, which establishes \cite[Conjecture~1.1]{KO2018} in these dimensions. The proof combines the classification of extremal contractions with constructions of nontrivial admissible subcategories. In dimension four, we refine the descriptions of isolated surface fibers and construct exceptional objects supported on certain fibers.

papers.title: Transition to turbulence in swirl created by a vertical magnetic field in liquid metal electrodes
papers.abstract: Flow transitions in electromagnetically-driven swirl in a cylindrical domain are investigated using three-dimensional simulations for a liquid metal battery electrode. The parameter space considered: applied current $I=11.11-100A$; Current density, $J_0 \approx 4,000-35,000 A/m^2$, domain radius, $R=3-9cm$, domain height, $H=3$ and $4.5cm$). The background magnetic field, $B_0$, strength is varied systematically from 0.1 to 20 G to characterize the route to chaos. Davidson et al. (2022) found the onset of chaos occurs around $1-1.5 G$ for aspect ratio $1/6$ and current of 100A, however, this is shifted to $16-17 G$ for a lower current of 16A and aspect ratio $1/2$. Across a range of geometrical configurations and forcing conditions, including variations in aspect ratio, current and current density, a consistent sequence of dynamical transitions is evident from phase portraits, FFT spectrum, 0-1 chaos test, autocorrelation function and correlation dimension. The flow evolution is by the Ruelle--Takens-Newhouse route to chaos, with the strange non-chaotic attractor (SNA) regime providing an intermediate state prior to the onset of chaos. In our results, it is observed that, for a fixed aspect ratio, the transition is governed by a dimensionless group, $Q_m$, representing the ratio of applied Lorentz force to viscous force. The critical value of $Q_m$ at the onset of oscillatory flow is found to be nearly invariant except when the domain height is varied. Moreover, our results follow the $Re \sim Q_m^{2/3}$ scaling law expected from torque balance moderately-forced electro-magnetically driven swirl flows.

papers.title: Point Corrections and Wall-Crossing Geometry on the Quintic del Pezzo Threefold
papers.abstract: We study wall crossing for ideal classes of rational curves of degrees two through five on the quintic del Pezzo threefold $X=V_5$. Wall exclusion and a uniform bound on the correction length rule out point corrections in degrees two through four on the outer segments of the negative zero-tilt-slope paths. In degree five a correction of length one occurs and gives rise to a second component of the good moduli space. For a rational outer stability parameter, this space is reduced and has exactly two irreducible components. The closure of the smooth rational-quintic locus is a normal tenfold. The other component is the smooth thirteenfold $X\times\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$. Its points represent the polystable objects $I_{E_L}[1]\oplus\mathcal{O}_p$, where the pencil $L$ cuts out a quintic linear section $E_L$ of arithmetic genus one. The scheme-theoretic intersection is the normal determinantal ninefold parametrizing pairs $(p,L)$ for which $E_L$ is singular at $p$. Along their common reduced singular locus, the principal component and the intersection have transverse models given by the cones of $2\times4$ and $2\times3$ matrices of rank at most one, respectively. We construct a small resolution of the principal component as the projectivization of a rank-five extension bundle over the blow-up of the Altavilla--Petković--Rota sixfold along its point locus.

papers.title: DREAM: Delay-Resistant Acceleration with Momentum
papers.abstract: With exact, delay-free gradients, Nesterov's accelerated gradient (NAG) achieves optimal $\sqrt{\kappa}$ dependence for $L$-smooth, $\mu$-strongly convex objectives, where $\kappa=L/\mu$; heavy-ball (HB) achieves the same scaling on strongly convex quadratics. In asynchronous and distributed settings, gradients can be inexact, with delays varying across workers and iterations. We isolate staleness using a fixed delay $\tau\ge1$, replacing $\nabla f(y_k)$ with $\nabla f(y_{k-\tau})$ at iteration $k$. Arjevani, Shamir, and Srebro establish a worst-case lower bound of $\Omega(\tau\sqrt{\kappa}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ iterations to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to0$. We show that for any fixed positive delay, neither NAG nor HB retains $\sqrt{\kappa}$-acceleration on strongly convex quadratics when updating every iteration, for any stable constant step size and positive momentum. We introduce delay-resistant accelerated momentum (DREAM), which decouples gradient-query extrapolation from momentum and uses explicit delay-dependent parameters. DREAM attains a linear convergence rate $1-\Theta(1/(\tau\sqrt{\kappa}))$ for all smooth strongly convex objectives as $\kappa\to\infty$, yielding complexity matching the delayed first-order lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Our proof combines characteristic-polynomial stability analysis on quadratics with an analytic Zames--Falb integral quadratic constraint certificate. We extend DREAM to smooth convex objectives, obtaining near-optimal iteration complexity up to logarithmic factors for sufficiently small target accuracy. Experiments on strongly convex quadratics and regularized logistic regression corroborate DREAM's accelerated condition-number dependence under delay, unlike NAG and HB, and suggest this scaling persists when parameters use a conservative bound on the true delay.

papers.title: Antenna-coupled microstrip summing network for wave-like dark matter searches
papers.abstract: A commonly used technology for axion and other wave-like dark matter searches is a microwave resonator. In such experiments, the detected signal strength depends on the coupling between the resonator and the microwave transmission line that delivers power to the amplifier. In Axion Dark Matter eXperiment (ADMX) and other cavity searches, this coupling is typically achieved using a compact wire antenna inserted into the cavity. While this approach is adequate for right-cylindrical cavities, it can become difficult to efficiently extract power from large-volume, multi-wavelength ($V \gg \lambda^3$) resonators targeted for higher frequencies, such as those designed by ADMX-VERA (Volume Enhanced Resonant Axion). Here, we present a solution based on a microwave slot-antenna array capacitively coupled to a microstrip "summing network," which coherently combines signals from multiple transmission lines into a single output. This summing architecture is adapted from designs originally developed for cosmic microwave background (CMB) detectors. We demonstrate the design and characterization of a new high-frequency resonator that employs this readout scheme in the $19-21$ GHz range. Finally we discuss the potential to reach Dine-Fischler-Srednicki-Zhitnitsky (DFSZ) sensitivity using multiple summing network cavities fitted into a large volume.

papers.title: Rotational Perturbation Theory for Magnetic Interactions
papers.abstract: We develop rotational perturbation theory for magnetic interactions in collinear and noncollinear systems, distinguishing prescribed rotations of exchange fields from constrained rotations of magnetic moments. At the full exchange splitting, we derive Green-function expressions for prescribedfield energy curvatures directly from perturbation theory, without invoking the local force theorem; constrained-moment curvatures additionally require the stationary magnetic response and are related to the inverse static susceptibility. We examine noncollinear pair interactions and planar and conical spin spirals, and derive the long-wavelength ferromagnetic spin-wave stiffness and, assuming adiabatic sublattice precession, the antiferromagnetic spin-wave velocity. Orbital-nonlocal magnetic potentials and correlated electronic response reveal further requirements for connecting rotational curvatures to collective magnetic behavior. As a practical extension, we project the complete transverse pair Hessian onto an effective scalar Heisenberg exchange and quantify the unreconstructed curvature. Biquadratic and three-spin examples illustrate why locally extracted exchange coefficients need not represent transferable bilinear interactions.

papers.title: Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling for efficient quantum trajectories in metastable open quantum systems
papers.abstract: Open quantum systems can display metastability, with multiple long-lived states coexisting. Examples include the bistability of bright and dim manifolds in nonlinear driven resonators, or the long-lived coherent states of opposite phases in parametrically-driven systems, the building block of cat-state-based quantum computers. Metastability often emerges at system sizes where density-matrix evolution is impractical. Quantum trajectories mitigate this issue by evolving wavefunctions rather than density matrices. Metastable states then emerge as attractors towards which the system rapidly relaxes until a rare switching event brings it to another attractor. Simulating them remains costly, as one must resolve fast intra-attractor dynamics over timescales long enough to gather switching statistics. To tackle this problem, we introduce the Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling (DiSLOU) method, which combines three optimization layers: (i) Switching among locally optimal unravelings that minimize the number of quantum jumps in each metastable region. (ii) Diagonal propagation: the no-jump evolution is accelerated by diagonalizing the non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian once per attractor. (iii) Local reduced eigenspaces: the no-jump state can be faithfully propagated in a truncated subspace of only slowly decaying eigenmodes. We benchmark DiSLOU on the driven-dissipative Kerr resonator, finding no measurable loss of accuracy and the largest speedup in the bistable regime, where standard trajectories are most expensive. We then apply the method to the more challenging problem of accurately simulating rare bit-flip events in the cat manifold emerging in a two-mode dissipatively stabilized parametric oscillator, obtaining a performance improvement of over one order of magnitude. An implementation of DiSLOU in Julia is available as an open-source package.

papers.title: Yang-Mills-Higgs Limits of Reflexive Higgs Sheaves
papers.abstract: For stable Higgs bundles, Hermitian-Einstein metrics can be obtained as limits of the Yang-Mills-Higgs (Y-M-H) flow. We study the algebraic structure of subsequential limits of this flow for reflexive Higgs sheaves over compact Kähler manifolds, without assuming stability. We prove that the limiting reflexive Higgs sheaf is isomorphic to the double dual of the graded sheaf associated with the Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration of the initial sheaf.

papers.title: Integrate the Reward, Don't Sample It: Window Likelihood for Interruptions and Backchannels in Full-Duplex Speech Models
papers.abstract: When a user talks over a full-duplex dialogue model, it must decide whether the user is interrupting (stop) or backchannelling (carry on). Post-training can improve this discrimination or change how readily it stops. In our GRPO runs the second dominates: no configuration lowers both error rates on more than one model, and two released checkpoints discriminate no better than their bases. We trace this partly to how the reward is estimated. The probability of stopping inside a short window is a known function of a few stop probabilities the policy emits, yet GRPO estimates it by sampling. A group of rollouts that all agree gives no gradient, even when all fail; the push on the stop threshold is strongest where the model is unsure, whichever outcome is right; and whole-rollout credit reaches decisions the reward never judges. Confining the credit to the window removes only that leakage. Window likelihood (WL) samples the words but integrates over the stop decisions, so the probability of the correct outcome is computed exactly and its logarithm maximised. On HumDial-FDBench, across four open models, WL gives the best F1 and lowers both error rates by more than their confidence intervals, without talking into silence.

papers.title: Absolutely universal projective embeddings of long-root geometries of orthogonal type
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split Chevalley group of type $B_n$ ($n \geq 3$) or $D_n$ ($n \geq 4$), let $L$ be its Lie algebra and $\Gamma$ its long-root geometry, namely $\Gamma$ is the line-grassmannian of the polar space associated to $G$. It is well known that $L$ hosts a projective embedding of $\Gamma$, called the adjoint embedding, which realizes $\Gamma$ as a projective variety in the projective geometry of the underlying vector space of $L$. It is also known that $\Gamma$ admits the absolutely universal projective embedding, which is such that all projective embeddings of $\Gamma$ can be obtained from it as projections. When the field $F$ over which $G$ is defined is finite, the universal embedding of $\Gamma$ is just the same as the adjoint embedding. The same is not necessarily true when $F$ is infinite. Indeed, as we shall prove in this paper, the universal projective embedding of $\Gamma$ lives in a direct sum $K\oplus L$ for an $F$-vector space $K$, the dual of which is isomorphic to the derivation space $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ of $F$, which in general is non-trivial. Accordingly, the adjoint embedding of $\Gamma$ is universal if and only if $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ is trivial, namely $F$ is either perfect of positive characteristic or algebraic over its minimum subfield.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes, complex null geodesics and singularity resolution in regular AdS black holes
papers.abstract: The black hole singularity is hidden behind its horizon, and it is difficult to determine whether it is resolved by quantum gravity or stringy effects. For an AdS-Schwarzschild black hole, it is known that the two-point function of the dual conformal field theory has a singularity associated with a null geodesic that bounces off the black hole singularity. In this paper, we investigate how the resolution of the black hole singularity is encoded in the dual conformal field theory by considering regular AdS black holes as regularized geometries. Using WKB analysis, we compute the quasinormal modes of regular AdS black holes and read off the dual two-point functions from the modes. We find that the singularity corresponding to the bouncing null geodesic for singular black holes is replaced by a smooth bump associated with a complex, rather than real, null geodesic. The location of the complex geodesic singularity is supported by analyzing the structure of the operator product expansion for the two-point function. Our results provide a holographic signature of black hole singularity resolution and clarify how information about the regular interior is encoded in boundary correlation functions.

papers.title: TQFT gravity dual to the orbifold groupoid of Narain code CFTs over $\mathbb{Z}_4$
papers.abstract: In a companion paper arXiv:2610.26610 , we classified the Narain CFTs obtained by gluing copies of the $A_3$ root and weight lattices along their $\mathbb{Z}_4$ discriminant group; for two hyperbolic pairs, this gives 22 even self-dual codes forming seven inequivalent theories at $c=\bar{c}=6$. Here we develop their physical interpretation and connections to 3d topological field theory. All 22 codes are topological boundary conditions of a single abelian Chern-Simons theory, whose invertible symmetries, including fractional $B$-field shifts, organize them into three orbits: free, mixed and torsion. Boundaries in different orbits are related only by gauging. We determine all gaugings of order at most four between the seven theories, by $\mathbb{Z}_2$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$, with explicit twisted partition functions, and follow their effect on the spectrum and current algebra. We classify the topological surface operators of the bulk theory and identify those implementing these gaugings. Codes of the same group type are related by an invertible bulk surface; for different group types, every relating surface is non-invertible, and we find the minimal quantum dimension of such a surface. We give the fusion rules of the condensation defects, and show that theories self-dual under gauging carry non-invertible duality defects. Finally, we apply the TQFT gravity sum over topologies at genus one. We give a direct proof of the handlebody sum for any number of hyperbolic pairs, and closed-form weights for the handlebody and torsion contributions. For two pairs, the handlebody sum is the uniform average over the free theories and the torsion topology contributes the torsion theory, together reproducing the uniform average over all gluing codes. For three or more pairs, the handlebody sum alone is not a positive combination of code boundary states.

papers.title: Two q-Deformations of Narayana Polynomials: Rogers Moments, Hankel Positivity, and q-Narayana Kernels
papers.abstract: We study two $q$-deformations of the continuous interpolation between type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana polynomials, both based on the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) functional. For the affine-moment deformation, we establish coefficientwise Hankel total positivity via a continuant criterion and determine Hankel determinants and extremal coefficients of minors. The Askey--Wilson basis deformation yields a basic-hypergeometric Narayana kernel whose row polynomials have simple negative zeros, strict interlacing, and $\gamma$-positivity after palindromic normalization. A $q^2$-Askey--Wilson integral gives a continuous-parameter moment proof of the Krattenthaler--Wachs super $q$-Narayana expansion; an ordinary-power expansion recovers Pan's Touchard identity. For $0<q<1$ and $\theta>-1$, we establish total positivity of the kernel triangle and strict total positivity of its associated square, extending Wang--Yang's results simultaneously in $(\theta,q)$. We also prove coefficientwise total nonnegativity through order two for endpoint triangles and give an exact triangular change of basis between the deformations. Finally, we identify Tevlin's dual super $q$-Narayana polynomials with a normalized kernel, derive the recurrence for their index-two $q$-$\gamma$ coefficients via Rogers-functional Pearson--Christoffel identities, and deduce total positivity of the dual triangles and strict total positivity of their squares.

papers.title: Least energy solutions for a quasilinear Neumann problem
papers.abstract: We study the existence of nonconstant weak solutions and the qualitative behavior of the least energy level for a class of quasilinear elliptic problems with Neumann boundary conditions of the form \[ -\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}(a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}u) +\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_s a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}uD_{x_j}u =g(u)-\lambda u \quad \text{in }\Omega. \] Since the associated energy functional is neither of class $C^1$ nor locally Lipschitz, the classical Nehari manifold method cannot be applied directly. We therefore rely on variational techniques combined with nonsmooth critical point theory. For $\lambda>0$, we prove the existence of least energy solutions and show that, under suitable assumptions, they are nonconstant for large $\lambda$ and constant for sufficiently small $\lambda$. Moreover, the least energy level tends to $+\infty$ as $\lambda\to+\infty$. In the indefinite regime, a key ingredient is a spectral decomposition of $H^1(\Omega)$ associated with the linear operator \[ \mathcal L_0u :=-\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}\bigl(a_{ij}(x,0)D_{x_i}u\bigr). \]

papers.title: How reliable are automated X-ray reflection spins of supermassive black holes? A methodological study of 41 AGN with simultaneous \xmm\ and \nustar\ data
papers.abstract: This is a methodological study: we test how reliable black hole spins from an automated, uniform reflection analysis are, not how spins are distributed. We fit one simultaneous XMM-Newton EPIC-pn and NuSTAR observation of each of 41 AGN with relxillCp, a distant reflector and a warm-Comptonisation soft excess, using quality criteria fixed in advance, 20 starting points, spin profiles scanned in both directions and two-dimensional (spin, inclination) grids. We test whether the relativistic reflection is detected, and test every result against four changes to the model, two sensitivity tests, two alternative models (a high-density disc and a lamppost corona) and simulations. The disc reflection is not detected in 21 of the 41 sources, and 5 sources pass all checks. Their 90% spin regions are 1 lower bound (NGC 4051, a*>0.75), 1 upper bound, 2 regions in separate pieces and 1 unconstrained profile; none is a two-sided interval. The accepted fits lie at 32-56 deg. No constrained region keeps its type under all of the inclination limit, the removal of pn data below 3 keV, and the two alternative models, so the spin depends on how the soft excess and the corona are modelled. In two accepted sources, including NGC 4051, the disc component is detected mainly below 2 keV rather than in the iron band. Of the 18 sources accepted by a previous version of this analysis without a soft-excess component, 14 are not accepted, 11 because their disc reflection is not detected; none of the accepted fits is now edge-on (10 of 18 before). In simulations with known spin the 90% regions contain the true spin in 0.82 of cases when the model is correct; fitting the previous model to spectra simulated from the new one gives spuriously high spins and, for one of two templates, edge-on inclinations. The sample is not complete, and we make no statement about the spin distribution.

papers.title: Fixed-Point Abundances and the Onset of Extinctions in Multispecies Lotka-Volterra Ecosystems
papers.abstract: I investigate the average and variance of species abundance distributions for fixed-point solutions to generalized Lotka-Volterra ecosystems. Two different analytical methods are constructed. First, I build up on the perturbative Random Matrix Theory approach developed in my earlier work [Phys. Rev. E. 113, L062202 (2026)], and formalize this method diagrammatically. The abundance average is given by a sum of planar diagrams with non-crossing vertex pairings which can be encoded as Dyck paths. This allows me to express the combinatorial factor multiplying perturbative terms at each order as Catalan and Narayana numbers, following which the abundance average is given by the latter's generating functions. In this way, the infinite perturbation expansion is exactly resummed in a closed-form formula. I have not been able to find a similar resummation for the abundance variance, however diagrammatic Feynman rules are expressed, following which the perturbative series can be calculated to any desirable order. Second, I do the same calculations using the cavity method, which gives closed-form formulas for both the abundance average and variance. For the average, the cavity formula gives the exact same result as the perturbative approach when the average interspecies interaction vanishes. When this is not the case, the two results are functionally different, however they are hardly distinguishable in their parametric range of validity. Comparison with numerical data indicate that the cavity result is more accurate over a larger parameter range.

papers.title: Finite Volume Convergence for a Heat Equation with a Measure-Valued Source
papers.abstract: Past work with Tom Seidman analyzed the spatial convergence order of the numerical finite element method applied to time-dependent diffusion-reaction equations with a measure-valued source term. For smooth source terms, the numerical method has second-order accuracy, but the non-smooth source terms introduce a limitation of the order that depends on the spatial dimension. This work in honor of Tom extends the analysis to the finite volume method in its clas- sical two-point flux form and shows that the regularity of the source term reduces the convergence order to 1 in two and 0.5 in three spatial dimensions which is reduced from the nominal second-order and depends on the space dimension. Computational tests with a point source modeled by a Dirac delta distribution exhibit the behavior predicted by the analytical results.

papers.title: 3D Global Climate Simulations of Synthetic Mars Warming
papers.abstract: Artificial warming via engineered aerosols presents a novel pathway to bypass volatile scarcity on modern Mars. Utilizing the Generic Planetary Climate Model, we evaluate the physical feasibility of aerosol-induced terraforming over a full Martian year (669 Sols). Unlike previous approaches that added aerosols to background dust or assumed continuous nanoparticle injection, we simulate the complete substitution of natural dust with a single-injection profile of radiatively active aluminium nanoparticles without continuous dumping.
