papers.title: Two Tiling is Undecidable
papers.abstract: We show that the following problem is undecidable: given two polygonal prototiles, determine whether the plane can be tiled with rotated and translated copies of them. This improves a result of Demaine and Langerman [SoCG 2025], who showed undecidability for three tiles. Along the way, we show that tiling with one prototile is undecidable if there can be edge-to-edge matching rules. This is the first result to show undecidability for monotiling with only local matching constraints.

papers.title: Entropic smoothing and gradient approximation for Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization
papers.abstract: Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization offers a framework for model fitting in machine learning under potential shifts in the data distribution. We study a regularized variant of this problem in which entropic smoothing produces a sampled approximation of the original objective. We establish convergence of the approximate gradients to subgradients of the unregularized objective as the regularization parameter vanishes, enabling convergence guarantees for stochastic gradient methods. We obtain qualitative convergence results under general assumptions and provide convergence rates under additional regularity. In particular, we prove rates for the convergence of the unregularized objective values, up to sampling errors, when the regularization level is decreased across iterations. Our analysis also yields results of independent interest on approximating the subdifferentials of maximum functions by gradients of their smooth approximations, together with growth-based lower bounds on optimal dual variables in Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization.

papers.title: An iterative tangential interpolation algorithm for model reduction of MIMO systems
papers.abstract: We consider model reduction of large-scale Multi-Input, Multi-Output (MIMO) systems using low-rank barycentric tangential interpolation on the frequency axis. Our scheme is related to the recently-developed Adaptive Antoulas--Anderson (AAA) algorithm, which is an iterative algorithm that uses concepts related to the Loewner framework. One feature of our algorithm is optimization of the interpolation weight matrices to minimize a proxy for the \(L_2\) system error. We use the freedom in interpolation point selection to provide multiple minimum-error-based algorithms with trade-offs between computational complexity and approximation performance. We prove that a weighted \(L_2\) norm of the proxy error system is non-increasing as interpolation points are added, and that the reduced-order system is stable whenever the original system is. Computational results are provided demonstrating the closeness of the proxy system and true system \(L_2\) errors. Comparisons with prior work demonstrate performance on par with standard model reduction methods.

papers.title: Exact module categories over $\mathrm{Rep}(u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2))$
papers.abstract: We give a complete list of indecomposable exact module categories over the finite tensor category $\mathrm{Rep}(u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2))$ of representations of the small quantum group $u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, where $q$ is a root of unity of odd order. Each of them is given as the category of representations of a left comodule algebra over $u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ explicitly presented by generators and relations.

papers.title: Perturbative and non-linear analyses of gravitational turbulence in spacetimes with stable light rings
papers.abstract: Some black hole mimickers, as well as black strings and other higher-dimensional spacetimes, exhibit stable light rings-regions where light or high-frequency gravitational waves can be trapped. In these regions, linear perturbations decay slowly, raising the possibility of nonlinear instability mechanisms. In this work, we study the cubic nonlinear wave equation as a proxy for Einstein's equations, using a four-dimensional model geometry that allows stable trapping. By employing a perturbative approach, we show that the nonlinear wave equation on the sphere with dissipative terms captures several features of the full nonlinear problem. This framework allows us to confirm a previous conjecture: all higher-order energy norms grow for arbitrarily small initial fluctuation amplitudes. Additionally, we analyze the system's mode spectrum at late times, revealing an inertial range dominated by a direct energy cascade. These findings further support the notion that spacetimes with stable light rings develop weak, high-frequency radiation hair, which will not generically lead to instabilities.

papers.title: Rubik's Abstract Polytopes
papers.abstract: We generalize the Rubik's cube, together with its group of configurations, to any abstract regular polytope. We discuss general aspects, and provide a description of the group of the Rubik's simplex in arbitrary dimension, and of Rubik's tori. We sketch an analogous argument for the Rubik's hypercube as well.

papers.title: An 'Experimental Mathematics' Approach to Stolarsky Interspersions via Automata Theory
papers.abstract: We look at the Stolarsky interspersions (such as the Wythoff array) one more time, this time using tools from automata theory. These tools allow easy verification of many of the published results on these arrays, as well as proofs of new results.

papers.title: Positivity of line bundles on general blow ups of Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate various positivity properties of line bundles on general blow ups of Hirzebruch surfaces motivated by \cite{Han}, where the author has studied general blow ups of $\mathbb{P}^2$. For each of the properties: ampleness, global generation, very ampleness, and $k$-very ampleness, we provide several sufficient numerical conditions.

papers.title: Efficient LP warmstarting for linear modifications of the constraint matrix
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of computing the optimal solution and objective value of a linear program whose constraint matrix changes linearly with a parameter, for a predefined set of values of this parameter. Based on the information given by a precomputed basis, we present three efficient LP warm-starting algorithms, based on the eigenvalue decomposition, the Schur decomposition and the Hessenberg decomposition, to evaluate the optimal solution and optimal objective value of these problems. The three algorithms have an overall complexity of $O(pm^2+pmn)$ where $m$ (resp. $n$) is the number of constraints (resp. variables) of the original problem and $p$ the number of parameter values after an initial preprocessing step. We also provide theorems related to the optimality conditions to verify when a basis is still optimal. When the perturbation of the basis matrix has a low rank $\rho$, as is often the case in practice, we then reduce all the computations to a $\rho\times\rho$ matrix built with $\rho$ solves with the factorization of the basis maintained by the simplex solver; with it, we compute, in each direction, an interval on which the basis is guaranteed to remain optimal, together with a bound on the objective. In practice, these intervals are close to the exact ones, and they remain useful for degenerate bases. We also propose a matrix-free method based on shifted Krylov subspaces. Numerical experiments on 398 instances built from real models, with up to 349,120 constraints, assess the accuracy, the cost and the range of applicability of all the methods. On the interval on which a basis remains optimal, once this interval is known, the low-rank and Krylov methods compute the optimal objective value 117 to 304 times faster than a warm start of the solver, in median.

papers.title: Colouring signed analogues of Kneser, Schrijver, and Borsuk graphs
papers.abstract: The Kneser signed graph $\KS(n,k)$, $k\leq n$, is the graph whose vertices are signed $k$-subsets of $[n]$ (i.e. $k$-subsets $S$ of $\{ \pm 1, \pm 2, \ldots, \pm n\}$ such that $S\cap (-S)=\emptyset$). Two vertices $A$ and $B$ are adjacent with a positive edge if $A\cap (-B)=\emptyset$ and with a negative edge if $A\cap B=\emptyset$. We prove that the balanced chromatic number of $\KS(n,k)$ is $n-k+1$. We then introduce the signed analogue of Schrijver graphs and show that choosing one representative from each antipodal pair of alternating signed $k$-sets gives a vertex-critical subgraph of $\KS(n,k)$ with respect to balanced colouring. For the Borsuk signed graph on $S^d$, we obtain balanced chromatic number $d+1$ for sufficiently small distance parameter and relate this equality to antipodal covers of the sphere. On $S^2$, spherical and projective covering bounds give three, four and six as the first successive values of the balanced chromatic number.

papers.title: Limits of harmonic functions on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
papers.abstract: We give an example of a sequence of positive harmonic functions on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq 2$, that converges pointwise to a non-harmonic function.

papers.title: Triangulations of the 3-sphere with knotted edge
papers.abstract: We prove that for any knot $K$, there exists a one-vertex triangulation of the $3$-sphere containing an edge forming $K$. The proof is constructive, and based on fully augmented links. We use our method to produce ``complicated'' simplicial triangulations of the $3$-sphere that we show are smallest possible, up to a constant multiplicative factor.

papers.title: On reality of eigenvalues of banded block Toeplitz matrices
papers.abstract: We formulate and partially prove a general conjecture providing necessary and sufficient conditions for the reality of the asymptotic spectrum of an arbitrary real banded block Toeplitz matrix. Additionally we present numerical experiments supporting it. This conjecture is a direct generalization of the already existing one in the case of banded Toeplitz matrices.

papers.title: Information geometric regularization of unidimensional pressureless Euler equations yields global strong solutions
papers.abstract: Partial differential equations describing compressible fluids are prone to the formation of shock singularities, arising from faster upstream fluid particles catching up to slower, downstream ones. In geometric terms, this causes the deformation map to leave the manifold of diffeomorphisms. Information geometric regularization addresses this issue by changing the manifold geometry to make it geodesically complete. Empirical evidence suggests that this results in smooth solutions without adding artificial viscosity. This work makes a first step towards understanding this phenomenon rigorously, in the setting of the unidimensional pressureless Euler equations. It shows that their information geometric regularization has smooth global solutions. By establishing $\Gamma$-convergence of its variational description, it proves convergence of these solutions to entropy solutions of the nominal problem, in the limit of vanishing regularization parameter. A consequence of these results is that manifolds of unidimensional diffeomorphisms with information geometric regularization are geodesically complete.

papers.title: Quandle Cohomology Quiver Representations
papers.abstract: We define a family of quiver representation-valued invariants of oriented classical and virtual knots and links associated to a choice of finite quandle $X$, abelian group $A$, set of quandle 2-cocycles $C\subset H^2_Q(x;A)$, choice of coefficient ring $k$ and set of quandle endomorphisms $S\subset \mathrm{Hom}(X,X)$. From this representation we define four new polynomial (or ``polynomial'' depending on $A$) invariants. We generalize to the case of biquandles and compute some examples.

papers.title: Transformation of Stochastic Recursions and Critical Phenomena in the Analysis of the Athreya-Aldous-Shields Cascade and Related Mean Flow Equations
papers.abstract: We study the discounted branching random walk process introduced by Athreya (1985) and Aldous and Shields (1988), referred to as the Athreya-Aldous-Shields (AAS) cascade. This process can be viewed as an idealized version of the stochastic model introduced by Le Jan and Sznitman in 1997 for the Navier-Stokes equations. The AAS cascade exhibits phase transitions at the critical branching rates $\alpha=1$ and $\alpha=2$. These transitions are reflected in the behavior of the associated mean flow equation, a nonlocal ODE referred to as the $\alpha$-Riccati equation. It is known that if $\alpha>1$, the AAS cascade is explosive in the sense of infinitely many splittings in finite time, and the $\alpha$-Riccati equation has at least two solutions. In this paper, we establish finer structural properties of an explosive AAS cascade and obtain a stronger non-uniqueness result. Namely, for each initial data in a certain range, the $\alpha$-Riccati equation has an infinite family of distinct solutions parametrized by their convergence rates at infinity. Our approach exploits a simple transformation between the AAS cascade and its "linearized" counterpart, whose mean flow equation is precisely the well-studied pantograph equation. This transformation demonstrates how a relationship at the level of stochastic processes can reveal an otherwise hidden relationship at the level of mean flow equations.

papers.title: Inertial forces and elastohydrodynamic interaction of spherical particles in wall-bounded sedimentation experiments at low particle Reynolds number
papers.abstract: Unsteady, wall-bounded sedimentation of spheres at low particle Reynolds numbers under the influence of small elastic deformation was investigated experimentally. The complete kinematics of elastic and rigid spheres sedimenting from rest at various initial distances from a rigid plane wall in a rectangular duct were measured. Several previously unrecognized phenomena arising from fluid inertia and superimposed elastohydrodynamic effects were identified and analyzed. Among these is an \textit{inertial wall attraction}, whereby particles migrate towards the wall during the initial acceleration phase. After this initial phase, rigid spheres sedimenting at $Re_\text{P}\approx O(10^{-1})$ followed behavior consistent with classic wall-lift models, including approximately linear migration away from the wall. In contrast, at smaller Reynolds numbers, $Re_\text{P}\approx O(10^{-2})$, both rigid and elastic spheres exhibited persistently unsteady sedimentation, characterized by deceleration despite increasing wall distance. These results enable the formulation of a conceptual framework that classifies near-wall sedimentation regimes according to particle Reynolds number and the position of boundaries relative to the Stokes length scale. For increasing deformability, the unsteady behavior was further modulated by nonlinearities. The observations suggest the presence of an \textit{elastohydrodynamic memory} effect arising from the coupling of fluid inertial forces with particle deformability. The experimental findings are supported by computational fluid dynamics simulations that provide qualitative insight into the evolving flow field. Overall, the results demonstrate that classic assumptions commonly applied to particle sedimentation in creeping flows break down in the presence of nearby boundaries...

papers.title: Positivity, cross-ratios, photons, and the Collar Lemma
papers.abstract: We prove that $\Theta$-positive representations of fundamental groups of surfaces (possibly cusped or of infinite type) satisfy a collar lemma, and their associated cross-ratios are positive. As a consequence we deduce that $\Theta$-positive representations form closed subsets of the representation variety. Along the way we systematically study a class of curves inside general flag manifolds that we call photons. Using their interplay with transversality in the flag manifold, we construct photon projections, which we use to relate the cross-ratios on the photons to the cross-ratios on the flag manifolds.

papers.title: On Sparsity and Sub-Gaussianity in the Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma
papers.abstract: We provide a simple proof of the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma for sub-Gaussian variables. We extend the analysis to identify how sparse projections can be, and what the cost of sparsity is on the target dimension. The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is the theoretical core of the dimensionality reduction methods based on random projections. While its original formulation involves matrices with Gaussian entries, the computational cost of random projections can be drastically reduced by the use of simpler variables, especially if they vanish with a high probability. In this paper, we propose a simple and elementary analysis of random projections under classical assumptions that emphasizes the key role of sub-Gaussianity. Furthermore, we show how to extend it to sparse projections, emphasizing the limits induced by the sparsity of the data itself.

papers.title: Fluctuations in the non-linear supersymmetric hyperbolic sigma model with hierarchical interactions
papers.abstract: We consider a class of non-linear supersymmetric hyperbolic sigma models on a hierarchical lattice. We prove that the hyperbolic distance between the superspin at any vertex and a reference superspin has asymptotically small fluctuations for large enough interactions, uniformly in the size of the graph and in the choice of the vertex. This can be viewed as a spontaneous breaking of the Lorentz boost symmetry.

papers.title: Post-Selection Inference for Partially Identified Parameters
papers.abstract: Partial identification of parameters such as average treatment effects, average partial effects and welfare is particularly common when using observational data and experimental data with imperfect compliance due to the endogeneity of individuals' treatment uptake. In this setting, the researcher is typically interested in a treatment or policy that is either selected from the estimated set of best-performers or arises from a data-dependent selection rule. In this paper, we develop new inference tools for partially-identified parameters chosen via these forms of selection. We develop three types of confidence intervals for data-dependent and partially-identified parameters, discuss how they apply to several examples of interest and prove their uniform asymptotic validity under weak assumptions.

papers.title: Exploring Optimal Transport for Event-Level Anomaly Detection at the Large Hadron Collider
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection is a promising, model-agnostic strategy to find physics beyond the Standard Model. State-of-the-art machine learning methods offer impressive performance on anomaly detection tasks, but interpretability, resource, and memory concerns motivate considering a wide range of alternatives. We explore using the 2-Wasserstein distance from optimal transport theory, both as an anomaly score and as the input to interpretable machine learning methods, for event-level anomaly detection at the Large Hadron Collider. The choice of ground space plays a key role in optimizing performance. We comment on the feasibility of implementing these methods in the L1 trigger system.

papers.title: Traveling waves of NLS system arising in optical material without Galilean symmetry
papers.abstract: We study a nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) system with cubic interactions arising in nonlinear optics, focusing on how the absence of Galilean symmetry affects solution dynamics. In the mass-critical case, we establish a new global existence result that contrasts with classical results. By exploiting the properties of traveling solitary waves, we obtain a condition on the initial data that relaxes the standard sharp assumptions. We also characterize the high-frequency limit of these traveling solitary waves as the frequency $\omega$ tends to infinity.

papers.title: Heat kernel estimates for boundary traces of reflected diffusions on uniform domains
papers.abstract: We study the boundary trace processes of reflected diffusions on uniform domains. We obtain stable-like heat kernel estimates for such a boundary trace process when the diffusion on the underlying ambient space satisfies sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates. Our arguments rely on new results of independent interest such as sharp two-sided estimates and the volume doubling property of the harmonic measure, the existence of a continuous extension of the Naïm kernel to the topological boundary, and the Doob--Naïm formula identifying the Dirichlet form of the boundary trace process as the pure-jump Dirichlet form whose jump kernel with respect to the harmonic measure is exactly (the continuous extension of) the Naïm kernel.

papers.title: Revealing the Nonlinear Amplification of Radiation Reaction Effects via Vortex Radiation
papers.abstract: Radiation reaction (RR), the back-action of emitted radiation on an accelerated charge, dominates the dynamics of ultrarelativistic electrons in an intense electromagnetic field. We derive an analytical formula for the RR-inclusive harmonic spectrum of vortex $\gamma$-ray emission in monochromatic-wave nonlinear inverse Thomson scattering (NITS), extend it to finite pulses under the slowly varying envelope approximation (SVEA), and take the Landau-Lifshitz (LL) solution as the starting point. We find that once cumulative RR on the oscillation radius over hundreds of cycles becomes non-negligible, the laser intensity nonlinearly amplifies RR through the modified longitudinal drift velocity, reshaping the vortex emission. For monochromatic approximation of long pulse flat-top laser, harmonic band acquire MeV-scale red shifts and spectral compression, producing overlap; higher harmonics show anomalous polarization transitions, so the superposed ellipticity departs from the RR-free case. For a $\sin^2$ envelope, the lower edge red-shifts while the upper cutoff stays fixed, broadening the band, and individual polarization transitions remain analogous to RR-free case. These harmonic-resolved spectral and polarization fingerprints constitute a self-referenced multidimensional diagnostic of RR effects that complements energy-spectrum measurements and, through the RR-inclusive scaling law between the polarization and laser amplitude, provide an independent route to measuring the laser intensity. These results have direct implications for bright high-energy $\gamma$-ray sources and the modeling of extreme astrophysical environments such as neutron-star magnetospheres.

papers.title: Killing Spinors for Finite Temperature Euclidean Solutions at the BPS Bound
papers.abstract: In a recent paper [ arXiv:2308.00038 ], Anupam, Chowdhury, and Sen conjectured that the finite temperature Euclidean five-dimensional Cvetic-Youm solution saturating the BPS bound is supersymmetric. In this paper, we explicitly construct Killing spinors for this solution in five-dimensional minimal supergravity. We also expand on the previous discussions of Killing spinors for the finite temperature Euclidean Kerr-Newman solution saturating the BPS bound. For both these cases, we show that the total charge gets divided into two harmonic sources on three-dimensional flat base space.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for optimal dividend problem under diffusion model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the optimal dividend problem under the continuous time diffusion model with the bounded dividend rate from the Reinforcement Learning (RL) perspective. Unlike the standard literature, our main focus will be on numerical algorithms that allow part or all of the system parameters to be unspecified so that the optimal control cannot be explicitly determined. Following the RL literature we introduce the entropy-regularized exploratory control problem, which randomizes the control actions and balances the levels of exploitation and exploration, and carry out a theoretical analysis of the associated Policy Improvement (PI) and Policy Evaluation (PE) devices and the corresponding sequence of the approximating optimal strategies. Specifically, our algorithm will be based on two independent neural networks that approximate the value function and its derivative simultaneously. Such an algorithm, to the best of our knowledge, is new in the context of the optimal dividend problems, and can be effective even for the situation when the premium and/or interest rate is state dependent, hence beyond reach of the standard statistical methods. Some numerical experiments are presented to empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of our RL algorithm.

papers.title: Testing the equality of the copulas of two multivariate populations with Bernstein polynomials
papers.abstract: The empirical Bernstein copula process is utilized to conduct tests for the equal- ity of the dependence structures between two samples. To this end, three tests statistics are proposed, and their asymptotic properties are established under mild regularity conditions. Furthermore, in order to obtain a valid p-value, sub- sampling and multiplier bootstrap methods are introduced and investigated for the Bernstein based-test statistics. Through a simulation study, it is shown that Bernstein-based tests significantly outperform tests based on the empirical copula.

papers.title: Online Nonconvex Decision Making with Approximate Oracles
papers.abstract: We study online decision making with possibly nonconvex (for example, combinatorial or integer) local feasible sets and convex long-term constraints. At each period, a decision maker selects a local action to maximize cumulative reward while ensuring that the sequence of actions satisfies the global constraints in the long term. It is known that $O(\sqrt{T})$ long-term constraint violation and $O(\sqrt{T})$ reward regret are achievable if given access to a local optimization oracle that exactly solves optimization problems over each local feasible set. Instead of requiring exact optimization over each local feasible set, we assume access to an approximate local optimization oracle that permits optimization errors quantified by two parameters $(\delta_+,\delta_\times)$. We develop an approximate online dual mirror descent algorithm and show that its guarantees depend on a feasibility slack parameter $\underline d$, which measures the compatibility between local feasible sets and the long-term constraint. Under the standard random permutation model, when $\delta_+=O(1)$, $\delta_\times<\underline d$ and $\underline d-\delta_\times=\Omega(1)$, the algorithm achieves $O(\sqrt T)$ long-term constraint violation and reward regret up to $O\bigl(\sqrt T+\delta_\times T\bigr)+\delta_+ T$. We also show a matching limitation: when $\delta_+=0$ and $\delta_\times>\underline d$, no online algorithm relying on such approximate oracle outputs can guarantee sublinear long-term constraint violation in general.

papers.title: Demystifying the characterization of SDP matrices in mathematical programming
papers.abstract: This manuscript was written because I found no other introduction to SDP programming that targets the same audience. A first difference compared to other existing introductions to SDP is that this work comes out of a mind that was itself struggling to understand. This may seem to be only a weakness, but, paradoxically, it is both a weakness and a strength. First, I did not try to overpower the reader, but I tried to minimize the distance between the author and the reader as much as possible, even hoping to achieve a small level of mutual empathy. This enabled me avoid a quite common pitfall: many long-acknowledged experts tend to forget the difficulties of beginners. Other experts try to make all proofs as short as possible and to dismiss as unimportant certain key results they have seen thousands of time in their career. I also avoided this, even if I did shorten a few proofs when I revised this manuscript two years after it was first written. However, I also kept certain proofs that seem longer than necessary because I feel they offer more insight; an important goal is to capture the "spirit" of each proven result instead of reducing it to a flow of formulae. The very first key step towards mastering SDP programming is to get full insight into the eigen-decomposition of real symmetric matrices. It is enough to see the way many other introductions to SDP programming address this eigen-decomposition to understand that their target audience is different from mine. They often list the eigen-decomposition without proof, while I give two proofs to really familiarize the reader with it.

papers.title: A Practical Route to Demonstrating Core Reactivity in Cs Polyoxides under Pressure
papers.abstract: Activating normally inert core electrons expands the bonding possibilities of elements beyond conventional valence chemistry. Although Cs core reactivity under pressure was predicted in polyfluorides more than a decade ago, experimental confirmation remains elusive, largely because loading highly corrosive F$_{2}$ poses serious challenges for diamond anvil cells. Here, global crystal structure searches combined with first-principles calculations identify Cs polyoxides as a practical alternative for investigating core reactivity. Compression activates Cs 5p electrons, leading to oxidation beyond the usual +1 state and a striking reversal of conventional polyoxide behavior: O-O bonds disappear, while strong Cs-O covalent bonds generate molecular units and extended sheets. Most importantly, CsO, a solid peroxide stable at ambient pressure, is predicted to undergo this transformation at 221 GPa, forming linear [CsO$_{2}$]$^{-}$ units. This approach replaces a chemical reaction between separate reactants with a phase transition in a single solid, avoiding F$_{2}$ loading and simplifying experimental implementation without changing the overall composition. The loss of peroxide O-O pairs provides a vibrational signature of the transformation, while calculated infrared and Cs L$_{3}$-edge XANES spectra, together with simulated X-ray diffraction patterns, guide experimental identification. These results establish an experimentally testable route toward core reactivity and show how pressure can extend the chemical possibilities of a familiar alkali metal.

papers.title: Convergence in Wasserstein Distance for Empirical Measures of Semilinear SPDEs
papers.abstract: The convergence rate in Wasserstein distance is estimated for the empirical measures of symmetric semilinear SPDEs. Unlike in the finite-dimensional case that the convergence is of algebraic order in time, in the present situation the convergence is of log order with a power given by eigenvalues of the underlying linear operator.

papers.title: Symbolic Control for Stochastic Systems via Finite Parity Games
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of computing the maximal probability of satisfying an omega-regular specification for stochastic nonlinear systems evolving in discrete time. The problem reduces, after automata-theoretic constructions, to finding the maximal probability of satisfying a parity condition on a (possibly hybrid) state space. While characterizing the exact satisfaction probability is open, we show that a lower bound on this probability can be obtained by (I) computing an under-approximation of the qualitative winning region, i.e., states from which the parity condition can be enforced almost surely, and (II) computing the maximal probability of reaching this qualitative winning region. The heart of our approach is a technique to symbolically compute the under-approximation of the qualitative winning region in step (I) via a finite-state abstraction of the original system as a 2.5-player parity game. Our abstraction procedure uses only the support of the probabilistic evolution; it does not use precise numerical transition probabilities. We prove that the winning set in the abstract 2.5-player game induces an under-approximation of the qualitative winning region in the original synthesis problem, along with a policy to solve it. By combining these contributions with (a) a symbolic fixpoint algorithm to solve 2.5-player games and (b) existing techniques for reachability policy synthesis in stochastic nonlinear systems, we get an abstraction-based algorithm for finding a lower bound on the maximal satisfaction probability. We have implemented the abstraction-based algorithm in Mascot-SDS (Majumdar et al., 2020), where we combined the outlined abstraction step with our recent tool FairSyn. We evaluated our implementation on the nonlinear model of a perturbed bistable switch from the literature. We outperform a recently proposed tool for solving this problem by a large margin.

papers.title: A Note on Decomposable and Reducible Integer Matrices
papers.abstract: We propose necessary and sufficient conditions for an integer matrix to be decomposable in terms of its Hermite normal form. Specifically, to each integer matrix, we associate a symmetric integer matrix whose reducibility can be efficiently determined by elementary linear algebra techniques, and which completely determines the decomposability of the first one.

papers.title: Holomorphic vector fields and rationality
papers.abstract: We prove Carrell's conjecture that a smooth complex projective variety with a holomorphic vector field having a nonempty finite zero set is rational. The proof uses slices for projective additive group actions and a birational invariant in the dimension-graded Grothendieck ring. For a vector field with one zero, we bound the second Betti number by the dimension of the kernel of the linear part at that zero. A multiplicative group that normalizes the additive action with a nontrivial character gives a product formula for the Betti numbers and a sharp upper bound for the Euler characteristic. We classify smooth projective surfaces admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero. Among smooth projective threefolds of Picard number one admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero, there are five isomorphism types.

papers.title: Unitary realization of wavefunction collapse
papers.abstract: Recent quantum reconstruction projects demand pure unitary time evolution which seems to contradict the collapse postulate. Inspired by Zurek's environment assisted invariance idea, a natural unitary realization of wavefunction collapse is proposed using Grothendieck group construction for the tensor product commutative monoid.
